statement: The bad-set spectrum cannot improve on the trivial bound |W_T^bad| ≤ N·p_bad, and the obstruction is structural rather than a matter of effort. Since 1_bad is not a character, W_T^bad = Σ_S b̂_S W_{S△T}. Two standard inequalities are available and both lose. (i) CAUCHY–SCHWARZ splits it as (Σ_S b̂_S²)^{1/2}(Σ_U |W_U|²)^{1/2}. The bad-set factor is (Σ_S b̂_S²)^{1/2} = √p_bad EXACTLY — Parseval for a 0/1 indicator, an identity with no slack — so no sharper knowledge of the spectrum can improve that side at all; every loss is on the other. That other factor is the UNRESTRICTED Walsh energy Σ_U|W_U|² = 2^{d−1}C_d, which is precisely the object dominated by the all-O tails of terminating starts that the bad restriction exists to remove. Writing C_d = K_all N² 2^{−(d−1)}, the route beats the trivial bound iff K_all < p_bad, and K_all ≥ 1 > p_bad always. Measured on 20000 exact orbits at y = 10^12: K_all = 8.81, 133.33, 532.30 at d = 12, 16, 18 against p_bad = 0.177, 0.127, 0.093, so the Cauchy–Schwarz bound divided by N is 1.25, 4.12, 7.02 — worse than trivial by 7× to 75×, and worse than the vacuous bound N itself from d = 16 on. (ii) HÖLDER against the Wiener norm gives ‖b̂‖₁·max_U|W_U| ≤ ‖b̂‖₁·N, worse still: ‖b̂‖₁ = 3.81, 7.75, 26.25, 57.65 at d = 8, 12, 16, 20 (L = 1.249), growing like 1.25^d, so ‖b̂‖₁/p_bad reaches 378 at d = 20. (iii) SPLITTING BY ORDER would rescue Cauchy–Schwarz only under low-degree concentration, and the spectrum is not concentrated — it spreads with depth. The fraction of ℓ² weight above order 2 rises 0.218, 0.269, 0.303 at d = 12, 16, 20, and 0.073 still sits above order 10 at d = 20, so a constant fraction survives every cut and the split gains a constant at best, never the exponential the tail needs. Only genuine correlation between the bad-set spectrum and the Walsh energy could win, and that is exactly what no bound on individual |W_U| supplies — the quantified form of the recorded remark that the restricted count is 'a bilinear form in the Walsh family weighted by the bad-set spectrum, strictly harder than the family itself'. CORRECTED AND NARROWED 6 Sep 2026 (adversarial review, three lenses). (a) Units: the comparison should be against the unconditional bound M, not N·p_bad, which is not free (see J-walsh-downweighting-survives-live); every conclusion survives a fortiori since the Cauchy–Schwarz bound exceeds M by the same margins. (b) Scope: what is proved is that no bound UNIFORM in T improves on M by more than a constant. The order-1 identity W_{{s}}^bad = (1 − 2q_s)·M, with badness forcing odd-heaviness, gives the floor max_T |W_T^bad| ≥ (2p_C − 1)·M − O(1/d), and 2p_C − 1 = tanh(θ_C/2) = 0.1988 at C = 20 exactly; measured 0.62·M at y = 1e12, d = 12. So a T-uniform saving on the characters is a saving on M itself — self-referential — and the kill covers Cauchy–Schwarz, Hölder, the order split, and every T-uniform bound. It does NOT cover per-order bounds: the aggregate tail Σ_{T≠∅} tanh(θ/2)^{|T|} |W_T^bad| is measured at 1.19·M against a trivial 6.35·M at d = 12 (gap 5.3×), and 2.91·M against 76.6·M at y = 1e20, d = 25 (gap 26×), the gap growing geometrically; from order 3 on the restricted sums sit at measurement noise. (c) A sharp per-character bound exists: under H(C,A) on bad cylinders, |W_T^bad| ≤ (N/2)(p_bad + |b̂_T|), from the counting identity #{w ∈ B : χ_T(w) = +1} = 2^{d−2}(p_bad + b̂_T); it is attained by an admissible count vector and survives imposing any collision count, so it is optimal among bounds using positivity, mass and H. Its gain is the factor (1 + |b̂_T|/p_bad)/2 ∈ [1/2, 1), a proved ceiling of 2, and no exponent moves. The per-order question is J-walsh-restricted-product-shape, OPEN. SAMPLING CAUTION ADDED 2026-09-19, and it does not disturb the verdict. The Wiener figures above are quoted at d = 8, 12, 16, 20 for L = 1.249. At that level the free lengths below 21 are 4, 6, 9, 12, 15, 17, 20, and at a free length the bad set is a full cylinder so every statistic of it is bit-identical to the previous depth (J-empty-window-holds-at-every-level). So d = 12 and d = 20 are exact copies of d = 11 and d = 19: the four quoted Wiener points are three measurements, and the three quoted order-tail points at d = 12, 16, 20 are two. The growth is carried entirely by the rises, running 1.474 per rise against the 1.254 per depth this row quotes as 'growing like 1.25^d'; both numbers are true of the same data and describe different things. The refutation stands unchanged -- the norm does rise, and it rises at every rise -- but anyone re-measuring on this grid should fit per rise, which is the caution J-good-set-wiener-norm-carries-the-rotation already carries and this row did not. Pinned in tests/research/juggler_sequence/test_empty_window_levels.py. MECHANISM NOW PROVED, 2026-09-19: the freeze this caution rests on was enumeration when it was written. Problems.Juggler.sum_aliveWordsAt_succ_of_window_empty proves it at level c: at a free length the alive set is a full cylinder extension, so EVERY additive functional of it is unchanged, not merely the Wiener norm. The frozen depths are that theorem, not a coincidence of the statistic chosen.

Capping the barrier profile at m = cap biases the measured log rate by -pi^2 s(1-s)/(2 cap^2) -- predicted before measurement, confirmed to one part in ten thousand. WHY. The cap drops the mass that would cross it, which is an absorbing wall; the barrier at m = 0 is another. A drift-free walk of step variance s(1-s) killed at both ends of an interval of length cap decays pi^2 s(1-s)/(2 cap^2) per step faster than the free walk. That the wall matters at all is the non-normality: the profile holds less than 1e-100 of its mass near the cap, but the left eigenvector grows like (1/r*)^m exactly as fast as the right one decays, so the product controlling eigenvalue sensitivity is flat in m and the wall counts as much as the bulk. CONFIRMED WITHOUT THE LIMIT. (4/3) cap^2 (r(cap) - r(2cap)) cancels the limit and so measures the coefficient alone: 1.12153, 1.13511, 1.14206 at caps 40 to 320 for the 306/485 barrier, extrapolating to 1.14900 against a predicted 1.149108. It tracks the slope and is not some constant near 1.149 -- the 11/19 barrier at s = 0.5789 extrapolates to 1.20283 against its own predicted 1.202943. CONSEQUENCE. The spectral gap is three times this, the Dirichlet modes going as k^2, so convergence costs about 10 cap^2 STEPS whatever q is -- which is 10 cap^2 / q sweeps, the trap recorded in the journal for 2026-09-15. Machinery: barrier_truncation_bias.

The quasi-stationary rate against a barrier of slope s is s^(-s)(1-s)^(s-1)/2, and the DENOMINATOR of a rational barrier leaves no trace on it. THE CLAIM. chernoff_rate is not a constant of the problem but chernoff_rate_at(BETA); the closed form holds at every slope, the barrier entering the large-deviation cost only through its slope. THE MEASUREMENT. The exactly periodic barrier ceil(t p/q) is iterated to its Perron eigenvector and the cap dependence removed by Richardson over three doubling caps. What is left, against log chernoff_rate_at(p/q), lies between -6.8e-9 and -7.7e-9 for every barrier tried -- denominators 3 to 485, slopes 0.579 to 0.684 -- and falls by 16 when the caps double, so it is the extrapolation's own O(cap^-4) floor rather than a property of any barrier. NO DENOMINATOR DEPENDENCE. Across the convergents 12/19 to 306/485 the denominator ranges over a factor of 25 while the residual is constant to 2e-12; at the single denominator 19, moving the numerator instead moves it by 1e-9, five hundred times more, and monotonically in the slope. CONSEQUENCE FOR BETA. The convergents approach log rho through |BETA - p/q| alone, at the rate fixed by J-rate-slope-derivative-is-the-tilt. BETA's large partial quotient a_10 = 23 is therefore invisible to the rate: it makes 665/1054 an unusually good barrier, which helps, and there is no arithmetic resonance to find. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE. Only the rate. psi is a different object, and the divisors still enter it through f_hat in the coboundary of J-log-psi-is-a-coboundary-over-the-rotation. Together with J-quasi-stationary-convergence-is-not-diophantine, which finds no excess at the convergent denominators in the cocycle's convergence, this closes the two approaches to the question that do not require controlling f_hat directly, and both come back negative. Machinery: chernoff_rate_at, rational_barrier_rate_limit.

The natural coupling proof for the quasi-stationary limit does not close: restricting to the light-tail class gives an invariant cone but no contraction. THE CONE IS INVARIANT, EXACTLY, and for a reason with no content beyond addition -- the updated value at a site is an average of two neighbouring old values, so the bound at the two sites adds. `update_true_ratio` and `update_false_ratio` prove pi(m+1) <= s pi(m) is carried forward by both updates in the bulk, at every s, kernel-clean. IT FAILS AT THE BARRIER AND ONLY THERE. A non-rising step sends mass up, so the updated ratio at m = 0 is at least 1 and no cone with s < 1 survives it (`boundary_ratio_at_least_one`). The defect is one site wide: measured, the bulk ratios sit at the initial value to four decimals while the ratio at m = 0 oscillates over 0.45, 1.45, 0.86, 1.67. BIRKHOFF STILL FAILS. On the light-tail class the Hilbert projective metric does decay to zero -- 6.22 to 0.011 and 23.92 to 0.0055 over d = 0 to 12000 -- but POLYNOMIALLY, not geometrically. Fitting log d_H against d and against log d over d = 2000..12000 gives residual standard deviations 0.20 and 0.011, a factor of twenty in favour of the polynomial, with exponents -1.865, -1.962, -1.606. An earlier reading of the same data over d <= 2000 showed the local exponent RISING, 0.74 to 1.90, which looks like eventual geometry and is transient; the longer window settles at d^-2. So the cone restriction does not restore the contraction that J-no-exponential-weight-restores-the-gap denies, and this is that same criticality seen from the projective side. WHAT SURVIVES. d_H is summable at d^-2, and a summable non-contractive argument is a different proof from Birkhoff -- it needs the polynomial rate as an input rather than producing it, which is the original problem. The invariant cone stands as the structure such an argument would use. No bound moves and no fate is excluded.

R(phi) is piecewise constant, changing exactly at the rotation orbit -- the same orbit psi jumps on -- and that explains why the single-jump model of f fails. THE ARGUMENT. The backward word has w_j(phi) = 1{frac(phi - (j+1)BETA) >= 1 - BETA}, and the set of phi satisfying that is an arc of length BETA with endpoints j BETA and (j+1) BETA. So a length-K word flips only at {k BETA : k = 0..K}, and is constant on every interval free of those points; Pi_phi, computed from the word alone, is therefore constant there too. R is a step function whose jump set is the orbit. VERIFIED. On a uniform grid of 8192 phases against a 1200-step word, R changes at 1100 grid steps, none of them strictly inside a gap, and no gap boundary without a change. Jump sizes decay: 0.1171 at k = 0, then 0.0358, 0.0179, 0.0089, 0.0068. WHY IT MATTERS. f = log(1 - b R / 2) - log rho inherits R's jumps on top of its own at 1 - BETA, so f is NOT a single-jump function. That is why measured |f_hat(q)| falls far below the pure-jump prediction |J|/(2 pi q), by a factor 37 at q = 84, and why the reading |psi_hat(q_j)| ~ |J| a_(j+1)/(4 pi^2) -- proportionality to the next partial quotient -- is NOT confirmed, its ratios running 0.03 to 4.7 across the convergents. That prediction is recorded as refuted in the form stated; a version accounting for R's own jumps is untested. NEW MACHINERY, WITH ITS LIMIT STATED. boundary_fraction_at_phases computes R at ARBITRARY phases rather than along the orbit, which removes the turn-count ceiling of J-psi-bounded-only-at-resolvable-resonances. But its convergence is slower than the d^(-2) of J-killed-walk-forgets-polynomially: against the exact forward profile the relative error runs 0.119, 0.037, 0.019, 0.008 at steps = 300, 900, 1500, 2500, about steps^(-1.5), so a few thousand steps buys about a percent. That is ample for locating structure and NOT ample for amplitudes, since the Fourier coefficients at deep resonances are smaller than the error. The deep resonance question therefore remains open, and the grid does not settle it. IN LEAN. The argument above is now machine-checked. `backWord_iff_fract_lt` is the whole of it: the letter, written against the anchor (j+1)*b, holds exactly when fract (phi - j*b) < b, so it is the indicator of an arc anchored at j*b. From that, `backWord_of_mem_arc` gives the letter on over [j*b, (j+1)*b) and `not_backWord_of_mem_gap` gives it off over [(j+1)*b, j*b + 1), which are the two arcs the orbit cuts; `backWord_congr` says the letter sees the phase only through its position relative to the anchor. All print [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. What is NOT formalised is the step from the word to R -- that needs the profile, hence the convergence that J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate still lacks -- so the Lean covers the exact half of this row and not the measured half.

The conditional law of the killed walk has a phase-indexed quasi-stationary limit, and rho is recovered from its boundary value by ergodic averaging. This is a better coordinate than psi in every respect measured. THE COLLAPSE. Conditioned on survival, the law of m_d = o_d - ceil(d BETA) depends on the depth only through frac(d BETA): two disjoint depth windows, d in [5000,12000) and [12000,20000), agree to 5.1e-4 across every m and every phase bin. That is an order of magnitude tighter than psi's collapse, for a structural reason -- pi is a conditional law, so rho^d d^(-3/2) cancels and there is no 1+o(1) to outrun. The shape varies with the phase rather than merely rescaling: Pi_phi(0) runs 0.1846 down to 0.0750 across the circle, a factor 2.46, while Pi_phi(1) barely moves and the higher states rise, so mass migrates away from the barrier as the phase advances. R(phi) = Pi_phi(0) has a 24.9x signal against within-bin scatter, compared with 9.7x for psi. THE ERGODIC IDENTITY. P_(d+1) = P_d (1 - b_d R_d / 2) is exact and proved by J-count-recursion-is-the-boundary-mass, so (1/D) log P_D is a Birkhoff average of log(1 - b R / 2) along the rotation and also tends to log rho. Unique ergodicity of an irrational rotation then forces log rho = integral over the circle of log(1 - b(phi) R(phi) / 2), the integrand vanishing below 1 - BETA where b = 0. MEASURED: the direct Birkhoff average gives -0.034924, -0.034827, -0.034792 over d >= 1000, 5000, 10000 against log rho = -0.034688185, closing as the window deepens; the circle integral of the binned limit gives -0.034717 at 100 bins, a difference of 2.9e-5, and exp(integral) = 0.9658769 against rho = 0.9659066. This is a genuine constraint rather than a restatement, since rho is independently known in closed form as BETA^(-BETA)(1-BETA)^(BETA-1)/2 by J-paper-b-tilt-reduction-and-the-phase-factor. WHAT REMAINS UNPROVED is exactly one link: the convergence R_d -> R(frac(d BETA)), which is the quasi-stationary statement. The recursion is proved and the ergodic theorem is classical, so the open analytic content of this whole thread now sits in a single named object -- the quasi-stationary distribution of a walk killed at a Sturmian barrier -- rather than in the existence of an almost-periodic prefactor. Machinery: boundary_fraction_profile, which returns R_d and optionally the conditional shape.

R is a jump function of the barrier SLOPE: discontinuous at every rational, continuous from the right, with jumps decaying faster than the threshold that would make its variation infinite. THE OBJECT. Fix phase 0 and vary the slope s; R(s) is the boundary fraction of the profile for the barrier ceil(m s). This is the SLOPE variable and not the phase variable of J-boundary-fraction-is-a-step-function-on-the-orbit; the two are different statements about the same coordinate of J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate, and neither is about psi's own bounded variation, which J-psi-is-bounded-variation-with-an-ostrowski-spectrum settled separately. RIGHT-CONTINUOUS, AND FORCED. The profile at phase 0 depends only on the past m < 0, where m s DEcreases as s grows; so ceil(m s) is right-continuous in s there and R inherits it. At 12/19, approaching from above lands within 3e-6 of R(12/19) and from below within 3e-6 of a value 7.0e-4 lower. THE LEFT LIMIT, AT PERIOD q. For s just below p/q the past barrier is floor(m p/q) + 1, so the past word is the FLOOR word -- carrying one exception at m = -1, where ceil(0) = 0 exactly -- and the limit is that word's fixed point advanced to position q-1 and given a single non-rising step. It matches a genuine approach through rationals to 1e-7 at 12/19, 29/46 and 41/65. Reading the floor word at position 0 instead returns 0.1876 where the truth is 0.0740, a factor of 2.5, which is how the misalignment was caught. THE SIZE. Crossing p/q moves the barrier at every negative multiple of q at once, which is what sets the q^-2 scale; the numerator fixes the slope, which sets the coefficient on it. c = jump * q^2 reads 0.228, 0.190, 0.150, 0.112, 0.083 at q = 100, 200, 400, 800, 1600, for local exponents 2.27, 2.34, 2.42, 2.44 -- rising, not settling. This matters because summing a jump c q^-2 over the rationals of an interval gives sum phi(q) c / q^2, which is sum c / q up to a constant and log-divergent at fixed c; a decaying c is exactly what makes the variation of R in the slope summable. NOT AN ASYMPTOTIC CLAIM: past q about 1000 the cap sets disagree -- 3 percent at 1600, 20 percent at 3200 -- so the exponent's limit is not measured here, only that it exceeds 2 wherever the computation is trustworthy. c IS ALSO A FUNCTION OF THE SLOPE, vanishing at s = 1/2 (0.0001 at q = 60) and peaking near s = 0.68, so there is no single constant to quote. Machinery: boundary_fraction_at_slope, boundary_fraction_left_limit, boundary_fraction_jump.

Whether psi is of bounded variation is the sign of a Birkhoff average, and the average belongs to a cocycle whose top Lyapunov exponent is zero -- which is why no fit settles it. THE REDUCTION. BV holds iff sum |a_k| converges, where a_k is the jump amplitude at the orbit point k BETA. Writing h_k = a_k k, the recorded step ratios split by Sturmian letter pair: 1.066 for s_k = 0, 0.983 for s_k = 1 with s_(k-1) = 0, 0.932 for s_k = 1 with s_(k-1) = 1 (J-psi-amplitude-rule-is-second-order-in-the-sturmian-word). The letter-pair frequencies at slope BETA in (1/2, 2/3) are 1-BETA = 0.3691, 1-BETA = 0.3691 and 2 BETA - 1 = 0.2619, summing to one. So the Birkhoff average of log(ratio) is -0.001180, and a negative value means h_k decays exponentially and BV holds, while exactly zero means a_k ~ C/k and it fails harmonically. THE EXISTING DATA CANNOT DECIDE IT. Propagating the recorded standard deviations gives -0.001180 +- 0.007687: the uncertainty is 6.5 TIMES the value, straddling zero. That is a sharper statement of why the row is open than 'the exponent is a fit near the boundary'. AND THE MODEL IS WRONG ANYWAY, which is the useful part. Constant step ratios imply EXPONENTIAL decay of h_k, not the power law k^(-0.0917) the envelope fit reports; these are different functional forms. Over k = 20..69 the recorded h_k runs 0.87, 0.85, 0.79, 0.81, 0.80, 0.77, a ratio of 0.885, against 0.944 for the constant-ratio exponential and 0.893 for the power law. The power law fits and the exponential does not. WHY, STRUCTURALLY. The jump amplitude a_k is the 0-component of the perturbation vector v = Pi_(phi+) - Pi_(phi-) evolving under the TANGENT COCYCLE of the update, so a_(k+1)/a_k is that cocycle's growth. Its top Lyapunov exponent is ZERO, because J-killed-walk-forgets-polynomially says perturbations decay polynomially rather than geometrically. A critical cocycle gives polynomial decay at an exponent, not exponential decay at a rate -- so the BV question is a polynomial exponent straddling 1 and no fit over a 3.5-fold window in k can settle it. This is the criticality in a FIFTH guise, after the absent spectral gap, the transient Q-process, the polynomial memory loss and the degenerate tail spectrum. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is not more fitting. J-r-jumps-halve-at-the-sturmian-zeros gives one ratio EXACTLY -- R(phi + BETA) = R(phi)/2 at a non-rising step, so the jump halves exactly. The rising-step ratio is not a pure ratio: the update mixes the jump in Pi_phi(1) into the jump in R, so the tangent cocycle is genuinely vector-valued. Computing its exponent exactly, rather than fitting a_k, is the route. NOT SETTLED HERE and nothing is claimed about BV; psi remains discontinuous with observed jumps, as before. SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY by J-psi-jumps-are-summable-and-psi-is-bounded-variation. The conclusion that the recorded data could not decide the sign was right; the framing was not. It assumed the three step ratios are constants in k, which would make h_k decay exponentially, and derived a Birkhoff average from them. The ratios are not constants -- they are the short-window reading of an exponent that steepens -- so the Birkhoff average was computed from an artefact. The question was settled by measuring a_k exactly over a 150-fold window rather than by resolving the sign of any average.

How far back the barrier is disturbed is not enough to say what it does to R; the PHASE at which the disturbance lands carries the rest, and together they factorise. THE KERNEL. Let K(n) be the change in R at phase 0 when the barrier is moved by one at m = -n -- a swap of the adjacent rise letters there, so it exists only where the word turns. Then K(n) = n^(-2-eps) g(frac(-n p/q)). At consecutive n the values look like noise, ranging over a factor of three across a band of 20; sorted by phase they are two clean monotone branches. Which branch is decided exactly: a lowering bump (which raises R) needs b(-n) = 0 and b(-n-1) = 1, forcing frac(-n p/q) <= 1 - p/q, and a raising one forces frac(-n p/q) >= p/q, so the open interval (1 - p/q, p/q) carries no single-step bump at all -- over the whole period of 2585/4096, 1511 lowering and 1510 raising positions with none in the gap. In phase order the lowering branch gives |K| n^2 = 0.158, 0.145, 0.117, 0.101, 0.091, 0.060, 0.053 and the raising branch 0.362, 0.336, 0.264, 0.242, 0.213, 0.181, 0.163. This is the same orbit structure as J-boundary-fraction-is-a-step-function-on-the-orbit, seen from the perturbation side. THE EXPONENT. Held at one phase and swept in n, |K| n^2 still falls: 0.268, 0.246, 0.216, 0.175, 0.131 at n = 40..1024 on phase 0.75, and 0.101, 0.098, 0.072, 0.058, 0.047 at n = 71..1196 on phase 0.20, for eps of 0.22 and 0.27. So the memory decays strictly faster than the inverse square. Quadrupling the caps moves the n = 1024 point by 0.9 percent against a factor-two effect, so it is not the truncation. ADDITIVITY, which is what makes the kernel usable. Separated bumps add: the response to two agrees with the sum of the singles to within 0.1 percent at separations of 70 and more, degrading to 4 percent at separation 8. The interaction is local. CONSEQUENCE. Crossing p/q bumps the barrier at every negative multiple of q, so J-boundary-fraction-jumps-at-every-rational-slope is a sum of these, and the eps measured here is the same margin that makes that jump summable -- reached by an independent measurement. The two agree at the low end of the jump's local exponents, 2.27 to 2.44; NEITHER PINS THE ASYMPTOTIC VALUE. Machinery: barrier_bump_response.

THE LABORATORY'S MINIMAL-CERTIFICATE LENGTH IS THE STANDARD DROPPING TIME, and A020914's OEIS entry has said so since 22 October 2009. The comment, by K. Spage: A020914 'represents allowable values of the dropping time in the Collatz (3x+1) problem when iterated according to f(n) := n/2 if n is even, (3n+1)/2 otherwise, as tabulated in A126241', with one exception at n = 1 set to zero by convention. The laboratory has called A020914 'the admissible lengths' and 'the binary lengths of the powers of three' and had never used the words dropping time anywhere outside a quotation of an OEIS title. VERIFIED HERE THREE WAYS, in exact integer arithmetic, not taken from the comment. (1) The lengths carrying a minimal certificate, enumerated over all 2^d words for d <= 21, are exactly A020914 over that range. (2) For every 3 <= n < 20000, the parity word of n taken to its dropping time is a minimal certificate in the laboratory's sense, with zero failures. (3) Every dropping time attained over 2 <= n < 2000000 lies in A020914, with no exception; the A020914 values not attained in that range are a finite-range artefact, since a large dropping time needs a large n, and the unattained set changes as the range grows. WHAT IT OPENS. A126241, the dropping time of n, is the tabulation of this laboratory's own object at the level of individual integers, and the laboratory has never mentioned it. Hikawa's two new sequences A398447 and A398473 are the extremal dropping times on dyadic blocks, so they are about this object directly rather than adjacent to it. A022921 is the first-difference sequence of A020914, values 1 and 2, described in OEIS since 23 October 2009 as 'increments between successive terms of allowable dropping times'. THIS IS THE SAME FAILURE AS J-paper-b-survivors-are-oeis-a076227 one level along: the object had a standard name in the Collatz literature and nobody searched for it. Nothing mathematical changes. What changes is that a referee reading 'the binary lengths of the powers of three' is being told the construction rather than the name, and the name is the one the field indexes on. THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, added by a second session following the cross-references rather than the comment. A126241 is 'Dropping time of n in the 3n+1 problem', Christof Menzel, 8 March 2007, defined for T(n) = n/2 or (3n+1)/2 as the least k with T^k(n) < n -- our per-integer object exactly, and it carries the note that these are also called stopping times although that term is usually reserved for A006666. It cross-references A060412 and A060413, N. J. A. Sloane, 6 April 2001: the starting values that set RECORDS for the dropping time, and the record dropping times themselves. So extremal dropping times are prior art from 2001, and Hikawa's A398447 and A398473, reported as extremal dropping times on DYADIC BLOCKS, sit beside that as the per-block version rather than duplicating it -- worth knowing before anyone reads the September preprint, because it says what his numerics are numerics OF. ALSO RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE, since the point of the rule is that it gets run: the same search was applied to this session's own objects and came back empty. The OE fibre size H_m = 1,1,1,1,1,2,1,1,2,1,2,... and the fibre lower endpoints 1,3,5,7,9,11,15,17,19,23,... are in no OEIS sequence. That is weak evidence -- both are short-valued and a niche parametrisation -- but the searches were made rather than skipped. VOCABULARY COLLISION, added the same day after a peer followed A126241's cross-references. The one-sided constant-factor collision bound of J-collision-bound-half-exponent is not a restatement of H(C,A), and the separation is proved rather than merely underived. Paper C §9.3(d) shows that the pair-correlation asymptotic Σ_w #[w]² ≤ (N²/2^{t−1})(1 + (log y)^{−A'}) is equivalent, by Parseval and Walsh inversion, to polylogarithmic savings on every Walsh sum to depth d(y), hence to H(C,A) with another A. Two independent reasons that argument cannot reach the crude form. (i) It consumes the accuracy: with a constant K in place of 1 + (log y)^{−A'} one recovers only Σ_T |W_T|² ≤ K N², hence |W_T| ≤ √K N per character — no saving on any individual Walsh sum. That computation is about the UNRESTRICTED collision count, which for the Juggler map is false by a factor growing like 2^{d(y)} (J-collision-bound-half-exponent); the conclusion holds a fortiori, since the unrestricted bound implies the restricted one, so a failure to invert the stronger hypothesis is a failure to invert the weaker. (ii) The restricted sum admits no Parseval identity at all: 1_bad is not a Walsh character, and expanding it gives Σ_{w bad} #[w]² = p_bad·C_d + Σ_{T≠∅} 1̂_bad(T) Σ_S W_S W_{S△T}, a bilinear form in the Walsh family weighted by the bad-set spectrum, not a diagonal one. The separation is exhibited by an explicit configuration: put mass N·p_bad uniformly on half of the L-bad words, each occupied bad cylinder at twice its fair share 2^{−(d−1)}N, the rest of the mass fair on non-bad words. Then Σ_{w bad} #[w]² = 2N²·p_bad·2^{−(d−1)}, so the collision bound holds with K = 2p_bad ≤ 2, while every occupied bad cylinder sits at 2× fair and H(C,A) allows only fair·(1 + O((log y)^{C−A})). Conversely H(C,A) implies the crude form with K = 1 + o(1), via Σ_{w bad} #[w]² ≤ (max_w #[w])·N ≤ N²2^{−(d−1)}(1 + 2^{d}(log y)^{−A}) and A > C + e(C). So the crude form is a strict intermediate: H ⇒ crude ⇒ the Tao-type bound at half the exponent, and crude ⇏ H. It also meets the four conditions the preceding journal entry set out for a route to the almost-all bound — a mean and not a supremum, stated at depth d(y) → ∞, one-sided, and not drawing cancellation per cylinder — of which only the last corresponds to a proved obstruction in Paper C (§9.3(e)); the other three are shape observations, not necessary conditions, and are not Paper C's own framing.

If the depth-d(y) collision count restricted to L-bad words satisfies Σ_{w L-bad} #[w]² ≤ K N² 2^{−(d−1)} with K = O(1), then #{n odd in (y, 2y] : τ(n) > d} ≤ √K · N · 2^{−e(C)L/2}: the Tao-type bound of Paper C Theorem 8.3 at half the exponent. Proof: τ(n) > d forces word_d(n) to be L-bad (Lemma 8.1), so the count is Σ over bad w of #[w]; Cauchy–Schwarz against the bad-word count of Lemma 8.2, #bad ≤ 2^{d−1} 2^{−e(C)L}, gives the display. Half the exponent is bought back by depth: the least C rises from 20 to 30 unconditionally, and from 18 to 28 under the conditional exponent λ***, since e(30)/2 = 0.5270 > 0.5074 and e(28)/2 = 0.4784 > 0.4608 (e(29)/2 = 0.5027 does not clear it). Restricting to bad words is essential and not cosmetic: over all words the collision count is dominated by terminating starts sharing an all-O tail, the same tail that makes the unstopped moment too large. Cauchy–Schwarz is saturated when the bad mass is uniform, so the factor 2 is not removable at that step. Not a halt theorem: the collision bound is not proved. GRADED FORM. The exported hypothesis is the weakest member of a one-parameter family: Σ_{w L-bad} #[w]² ≤ K N² 2^{−(d−1)} 2^{−γ e(C) L} with γ ∈ [0,1] gives M ≤ √K · N · 2^{−(1+γ)e(C)L/2}, so the least depth constant runs C = 30, 25, 23, 21, 19 at γ = 0, ¼, ½, ¾, 1 unconditionally (28, 24, 21, 19, 18 under λ***). γ = 1 is the fair-coin value of the restricted count, since p_bad ≍ 2^{−e(C)L}, and at γ = 1 the Cauchy–Schwarz loss is fully absorbed and the depth constant returns to 19/18, at or below the unconditional 20/18, so no penalty at all. The Phase-0 census normalizes against that fair value, so what was measured is γ = 1 while what was first exported was γ = 0; γ = 1 is the operative hypothesis and γ = 0 the fallback that survives if the fair constant is not attainable.

A convergent's rise word errs in |s - s'| T^2 of its first T letters, a full power of T above the naive bound. THE NAIVE BOUND IS FALSE. One expects ceil(t*s) - ceil(t*s') to be monotone, so the two words differ at most as often as it moves, giving 2(T|s-s'| + 1) disagreements in [0,T]. That predicts about 2 errors for 665/1054 against beta out to T = 32000; the measured count is 12. The difference OSCILLATES rather than climbing -- it equals t(s-s') + delta(ts) - delta(ts') with each delta in [0,1), so it crosses back and forth -- and total variation does not bound the count. THE CORRECT LAW comes from the arc form already formalised as backWord_iff_fract_lt: the letter at t is a rise iff frac(t*s) lies in (1-s, 1), the two orbits separate linearly as |frac(t*s) - frac(t*s')| = t|s-s'|, and equidistribution integrates the straddling probability to sum over t<T of 2t|s-s'| = |s-s'| T^2. It saturates at T/2, where the words are independent. MEASURED against beta at 306/485, observed over predicted: 1.09, 1.05, 1.03, 1.02, 1.01 at T = 8000, 16000, 32000, 64000, 128000 -- a 16-fold range converging to one from above. Deeper convergents are pre-asymptotic because the orbit has not yet come near the endpoint: 665/1054 reads 0.00, 0.00, 0.31, 0.65, 0.81 over the same window, climbing to one. THE PREFIX LENGTH IS STILL q_(k+1), as classical Sturmian theory says -- the first error sits at 484, 568, 25780, 24726 for 306/485, 53/84, 665/1054, 15601/24727, alternating between q - 1 and about q_(k+1) + q with the side from which the convergent approaches. What the T^2 law governs is how fast errors ACCUMULATE after the prefix ends, not where it ends. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: it is the letter-level reason J-sturmian-driving-is-uniform-in-q holds. 665/1054 and 15601/24727 reproduce beta's word exactly out to t = 24726, so their forward runs are identical there and only their limit profiles -- fixed points of different periodic operators -- can differ, which is why their Yaglom constants agree to six digits at d = 4000 and only five at d = 32000. Machinery: sturmian_word_disagreements. No bound moves.

PROVED, and it closes the amplitude question in both cases at once. Let N_d count the words of length d with o_t >= ceil(t BETA) at every t <= d, let M_d count those of them with o_d = ceil(d BETA) exactly -- sitting ON the barrier -- and let b_d = ceil((d+1)BETA) - ceil(d BETA). The mirror of J-dominant-defect-at-walk-minimum. Write x_k = X_k − D_k with X_k = n^{e_k} the floorless composition. Every step map is increasing and the floor only lowers, so 0 ≤ D_k and, by convexity of x ↦ x^{3/2} and concavity of x ↦ √x, D_k < 1 + c_k D_{k−1} with c_k = (3/2)X_{k−1}^{1/2} on an odd step and c_k = (1/2)x_{k−1}^{−1/2} on an even one; hence D_k < 1 + Δ_k with Δ_k = Σ_{j<k} Π_{i=j+1}^{k} c_i. Each product is the derivative of the composed map x_j ↦ x_k, about (e_k/e_j)·n^{e_k−e_j}: this is the amplification A_j of iteration 5 with the sign of the walk increment reversed. At a RUNNING MINIMUM s of the exponent walk (u_t > u_s for all t < s) every e_j > e_s, so Δ_s is small, and (i) x_s ∈ {⌊X_s⌋, ⌊X_s⌋ − 1}; (ii) x_s = ⌊X_s⌋ whenever {X_s} ≥ Δ_s. In particular the fibre {n : x_s(n) = m} is an interval of consecutive integers (monotonicity), essentially {n : ⌊n^{e_s}⌋ = m}, of length (1/e_s) m^{1/e_s − 1}, and the whole continuation x_{s+1}, …, x_d is a function of m alone. An even step absorbs the floor before it exactly, ⌊√⌊a⌋⌋ = ⌊√a⌋, so for the prefixes O E^j the state is ⌊n^{3/2^{j+1}}⌋ with no exception. Verified on 19615 live orbits at y = 1e20, depth 16 (100000 samples, seed 3): all 19917 running minima satisfy (i) (19842 equal, 75 one less); of the 19636 with {X_s} ≥ Δ_s all are equal (0 violations); the general bound 0 ≤ D_k < 1 + Δ_k holds at all 132796 steps checked with X_k < 1e40 (0 violations). Amplification and damping are one derivative with two signs, and the walk minimum is the seam between them: floors injected before it are damped to a single floor of the start, floors injected after it are amplified into the parity.

Along a Juggler orbit write x_k = X_k − D_k with X_k = n^{e_k} the floorless composition, e_k = 3^{o_k}/2^k = 2^{u_k}. The defect θ_k = {x_{k−1}^{3/2}} or {√x_{k−1}} injected when x_k is formed reaches x_{T−1} multiplied, to leading order, by A_k = Π_{j=k}^{T−2} m_j with m_j = (3/2)x_j^{1/2} on an odd step and (1/2)x_j^{−1/2} on an even one — the derivative of the composed map x_k ↦ x_{T−1}, which is x ↦ x^{e_{T−1}/e_k} — so that A_k ≈ (e_{T−1}/e_k)·x_{T−1}/x_k ≈ (e_{T−1}/e_k)·n^{e_{T−1}−e_k}, and D_{T−1} = Σ_k θ_k A_k. Three consequences. (i) A_k is decreasing in e_k, so the DOMINANT defect is the one injected at the WALK MINIMUM k* = argmin_k u_k: measured on 58869 live orbits at y = 1e20, depth 16, the argmax of A_k is the walk minimum in 100.0% of cases (100.0% under the θ_20 tilt), and the law's residual is +0.00/+0.30/+0.65 in log₁₀ at the 10/50/90th percentiles (median log₁₀ A_{k*} = 26.3, 90th percentile 300). (ii) θ_k is active for the parity of x_T — enters D_{T−1} mod 1 with A_k ≥ 1 — iff u_k ≤ u_{T−1}, the steps at which the walk was at or below its final value; for a meander ending high that is most of them: median 9 of 15, tilted mean 10.1. So the last-step phase is ONE object in size and Θ(T) objects mod 1; the nesting count is not reduced by the hierarchy. (iii) The dominant defect is injected where the prefix is at its most contracting and its image {x_{k*−1}} at its densest, and the parity of x_T probes θ_{k*} at scale 1/A_{k*} = n^{−(e_{T−1}−e_{k*})}, tilted-mean exponent Δe = 10.9 (10/50/90: 0.07/1.27/14.7), while the discrepancy of {m^{3/2}} over that image — of size ≈ n^{e_{k*−1}} — resolves at best n^{−e_{k*−1}/2}, tilted-mean exponent 0.70. The requirement exceeds the resolution by n^{10.2} on tilted average, 10^205 at y = 1e20. This is Paper B's growing-sawtooth obstacle located and priced: the amplification that makes the parity fair in fact is exactly what puts it beyond any equidistribution bound on the defect that carries it. The walk's climb from its minimum, e_{T−1} − e_{k*}, is the single number that measures both.

G(1) closes in the ladder height and stops there, for a structural reason rather than for want of effort. By duality, reversing (S_1,...,S_n) turns {S_k >= 0 for all k <= n} into {S_n = max_j S_j}, so sum_n z^n E[e^{-theta S_n}; stay >= 0] is the renewal series of the weak ascending ladder, 1/(1 - E[z^{T+} e^{-theta H+}]). The tilted walk is mean-zero hence recurrent, T+ is finite a.s., and at z = 1 this gives G(1) = 1/(1 - E[e^{-theta H+}]) with H+ the first weak ascending ladder height, which lies in [0, A) because the step that first reaches 0 is +A and the walk sat in [-A, 0) before it. With G(1) = 7.069 from the series (J-paper-b-meander-constant-derived) this pins E[e^{-theta H+}] = 0.85854. THAT IS AS FAR AS IT CLOSES, and the obstruction is identified rather than assumed. H+ is the overshoot of a renewal process whose two step sizes have irrational ratio A/B = log(3/2)/log 2 = log2(3) - 1, so its law is an equidistribution object governed by that constant's continued fraction, with no elementary closed form. The continued fraction is the same one, to its tail, as BETA's: A/B is [0; 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 5, 2, 23, ...], log2(3) is [1; 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 5, 2, 23, ...] and BETA is [0; 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 5, 2, 23, ...], sharing the tail 1, 2, 2, 3, 1, 5, 2, 23. So the obstruction to a closed G(1) is the same Diophantine structure that makes c_d oscillate and makes the least-peak staircase step at semiconvergent denominators (J-least-peak-staircase-is-beta-ostrowski). The chain is therefore: constant = kappa G(1) with kappa closed, G(1) = 1/(1 - E[e^{-theta H+}]) exactly, and E[e^{-theta H+}] a Diophantine quantity computed to five figures and not expressible in elementary terms. No bound moves.

What is actually governing it is the descending-ladder renewal function, which is positive at the origin rather than vanishing there -- the same ladder object behind G(1) (J-g-of-one-is-a-ladder-transform-and-stops-there). The criticality of the killed walk is not a coordinate artifact: no exponential weight separates the decay rate from the essential spectrum, so a contraction argument in that whole class is impossible rather than merely missing. THE CLAUSE THIS PROVES. J-killed-walk-forgets-polynomially says the memory loss is not geometric, so a contraction argument does not describe the walk HOWEVER IT IS SET UP. The quantified clause was an observation; this proves it for the class it is usually meant against, exponential reweighting. THE SET-UP, which is modelling and is NOT proved. On the space weighted by r^m the two updates act on r^m by multiplication, by (1 + 1/r)/2 and (1 + r)/2, so the log essential spectral radius at weight r is the beta-average chi(r) = (1-beta) log((1+1/r)/2) + beta log((1+r)/2). Identifying exp(chi(r)) with the essential radius is the modelling step; the theorem is the inequality about chi. THE THEOREM. `no_weight_separates` gives logRho beta <= chi r for every r > 0, and `chi_tailRoot_eq` gives equality at r = tailRoot beta = (1-beta)/beta. Since logRho beta IS the decay rate, the Perron eigenvalue never drops below the essential radius at any weight; the best an exponential weight achieves is EQUALITY, and it achieves it at the tail base the profile already carries, so the weight buys nothing the profile did not already have. THE PROOF, short because the pieces existed. Substituting r = exp s collapses chi onto the Chernoff exponent at the COMPLEMENTARY slope, chi(exp s) = chernoffExp s (1-beta) (`chi_eq_chernoffExp`); logRho is symmetric under b -> 1-b (`logRho_symm`), so the target is its own minimum; and the gap between a Chernoff exponent and that minimum is a relative entropy, chernoffExp lam b - logRho b = klDiv b (e^lam/(1+e^lam)) (`chernoffExp_sub_logRho`), nonnegative by Gibbs -- `OneSided.klDiv_nonneg`, already in the fate layer. No new analysis; what is new is that the three fit. All six declarations print [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. SUPPORTING MEASUREMENT. The capped period operator's gap CLOSES as the cap grows, |lambda2/lambda1| = 0.1079, 0.5701, 0.8683, 0.9652, 0.9912 at caps 40 to 640, which is what an essential radius equal to the Perron eigenvalue looks like from inside a truncation. And chi(r*) - logRho(beta) = 5.6e-17 with the minimum over a 400000-point scan of r in (0,4] nonnegative to 2.1e-12. CONSEQUENCE, and the limit of it. This closes contraction in the exponentially weighted class for the quasi-stationary limit of J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate. A weight w has local ratios w(m+1)/w(m); the essential radius is an average of chi over those ratios, and no average of values bounded below by log rho falls below log rho. PROVED, and elementary. Write N_d for the number of words of length d with o_t >= ceil(t BETA) at every t <= d, and P_d = N_d/2^d. If the barrier does not rise at step d, that is ceil((d+1)BETA) = ceil(d BETA), then N_(d+1) = 2 N_d and so P_(d+1) = P_d EXACTLY. Proof: let w be a surviving word of length d and x any letter. The odd count is monotone, so o_(d+1) = o_d + x >= o_d >= ceil(d BETA) = ceil((d+1)BETA), and w ++ [x] survives; conversely a survivor of length d+1 restricts to one of length d. So (w, x) -> w ++ [x] is a bijection from survivors of length d times two letters onto survivors of length d+1. THIS SETTLES J-sturmian-zero-step-leaves-the-raw-jump-invariant. When s_k = 0 both depths bracketing k BETA have a non-rising barrier, so P at each is individually unchanged under d -> d+1, hence so is any combination -- and the 1/rho of J-psi-amplitude-ratio-is-one-over-rho-at-the-sturmian-zeros is what the rho^d d^(-3/2) normalisation makes of one free step. CORRECTION. That row states that the two terms are NOT individually preserved and that a proof needs a bijection on their difference. Both are false, checked: at s_k = 0 each term is preserved on its own, to floating-point zero, and no bijection on a difference is needed or exists. The claim was asserted without testing it and is withdrawn. LEAN. The content is survives_succ_of_no_rise, with survives_of_survives_succ the converse restriction and noRise_iff_le_ceil characterising the non-rising step as ((t+1) b <= ceil(t b)), which for b = BETA is the Sturmian condition indexing s_k; barrier and barrierRise name the two quantities. Kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. The cardinality bookkeeping N_(d+1) = 2 N_d is the bijection above and is not formalised; it is one line and is stated here rather than in Lean. SCOPE. This proves an identity about the counting function, not anything about psi's existence, which remains a local limit theorem for a killed walk against a Sturmian barrier and is untouched. It also explains the residual drift recorded in the earlier rows: the measured ratios approach 1/rho from above and slide because of the d^(-3/2) factor, not because the identity is approximate. It is not approximate.

Three facts the Paper B barrier rows use, kernel-checked. (1) Mass: for a profile supported below N, the non-rising update preserves total mass exactly and the rising update loses exactly pi(0)/2, so no renormalisation enters a non-rising step. (2) Phase: for 0<b<=1 the barrier ceil(t b) does not rise at t iff fract(t b) != 0 and fract(t b) <= 1-b; at b = BETA = log 2/log 3 and t>=1, t BETA is never an integer (2^n != 3^k), so the barrier rises iff fract(t BETA) >= 1-BETA. (3) Count: prefixNoncontracting w iff o_t >= ceil(t BETA) at every prefix t <= |w|; the survivors whose E-extension contracts number b_d M_d, with b_d = ceil((d+1)BETA) - ceil(d BETA) and M_d the survivors with o_d = ceil(d BETA); hence N_(d+1) = 2 N_d - b_d M_d. These close the named Lean gaps of J-count-recursion-is-the-boundary-mass, J-non-rising-barrier-step-doubles-the-count, J-phase-shift-is-one-update-and-R-halves, J-psi-jumps-are-the-rotation-orbit-of-zero and J-r-jumps-halve-at-the-sturmian-zeros; their measurements and the amplitude recursion stay outside Lean, so those rows remain human proofs.

The cheapest non-contracting walk does not get arbitrarily high, and its ceiling is log2(3). Let P(k) be the least peak of the exponent walk over words whose walk stays at or above 0 for k steps. P is non-decreasing, P(2) = 2 log2(3) - 2 = 1.1699 exactly, and P(k) < log2(3) = 1.58496 for every k, approaching it: the gap is 7.5e-2 at k = 13, 1.65e-2 at 100, 7.5e-3 at 400 and 1.35e-3 at 3000, by a dynamic program over (steps, odd letters) rather than a search over words. The supremum has a reason: with c = log2(3) - 1, from a level u < 1 - c both E and OE are illegal, so the walk must take two odd steps and reach u + 2c; the levels a log2(3) - t come arbitrarily close below 1 - c, forcing a peak arbitrarily close to (1 - c) + 2c = log2(3), never equal to it since log2(3) is irrational. The measured gap to log2(3) agrees with the gap of the closest reachable level below 1 - c to three figures, which is the argument as a check. In exact terms the peak of e is in [9/4, 3). WHAT THIS CLOSES: the branch-run hypothesis of Paper B's screen fires at walk height 1, and P(k) > 1 for every k >= 2, so the threshold is always cleared -- that half is proved, `noncontracting_two_forces`. But the peak is bounded above by log2(3), so the emptiness of the screen at large depth CANNOT be proved by an argument of the form 'at depth d the walk must exceed T' for any T >= log2(3). Any route to that emptiness has to use where blocked defects sit relative to high points, not how high the walk goes. Measured to k = 3000; not a proof that P(k) < log2(3) for all k, and not a halt theorem.

Paper B section 7's composed map is the exponent walk of the Paper C collision work, and its linearisation criterion is a unit climb of that walk. With the notation of J-paper-b-defect-coefficient-chain, e_t = 3^(o_t) / 2^t exactly, where o_t is the number of odd letters up to t (`iter_eq_pow`). Taking log base 2 gives e_t = 2^(u_t) with u_t = o_t log2(3) - t, which is the walk J-live-set-ladder-factorisation splits at, J-damping-at-running-minimum is about, and J-dominant-defect-at-walk-minimum measures the climb of. Hence E = e_{t-1}/e_s = 2^(u_{t-1} - u_s), and E < 2 says exactly that the walk climbs by less than one unit between the defect at letter s and the wave at letter t. Two consequences. (i) The criterion is an exact integer inequality in the counts: with a odd and b even letters in the block, E < 2 iff 3^a < 2^(a+b+1) (`lt_two_iff_counts`), so it never needs a logarithm or a float. (ii) It does not see the order of the block, only the two counts (`iter_eq_of_counts`, `lt_two_congr`), which is immediate from the closed form and invisible in the product form; 45 count pairs cover every block arising in words of length up to 10. The supporting declarations are `oddCount`, `oddCount_cons_O` and `oddCount_cons_E`. Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. This is a reformulation and not an improvement: no bound moves, no density exponent changes, and the collision hypothesis is untouched. What it buys is that two screens developed separately are one test in one coordinate, and that E is literally the amplification factor A_k of J-dominant-defect-at-walk-minimum rather than an analogue of it.

Paper B's non-contracting word count and Paper C's bad-word count are one function at two levels. N_d of Proposition 7.1 counts length-d words whose walk u_t = o_t log2(3) - t stays at or above 0; bad_word_count(L, d) counts those whose walk never reaches -L. Both are the same dynamic program over (steps, odd letters), written independently in paper_b_prefix_count and collision_large_sieve, and N_d = bad_word_count(0, d) exactly for d = 1 to 16 (1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 13, 19, 38, 64, 128, 226, 367, 734, 1295, 2114). The agreement is exact and not approximate although one bound is strict and the other is not, because u_t = 0 would need 3^(o_t) = 2^t, which forces o_t = t = 0 (`three_pow_eq_two_pow`, `iter_eq_one_iff`, kernel-checked): the walk is never back at its starting level after a letter, so on a non-empty word the two readings of non-contraction coincide (`one_le_iff_one_lt`). The O-rooting costs nothing either, since a word starting E has u_1 = -1. TRANSFER, and its limit. Because the counts coincide, Paper C's tools apply to Paper B's object; the sharpest, the Wiener-Hopf ladder factorisation at the walk minimum (J-live-set-ladder-factorisation), does specialise correctly and computes with exact identity error 0 at L = 0.05 and 0.25. But it degenerates there: at L -> 0 the argmin sits at the start with probability 1, so every word is a positive excursion and the split has no descending side. The transfer is valid and empty at Paper B's level, which is worth recording so it is not attempted twice. Not a bound and not an improvement to either paper.

Paper B section 7's per-letter coefficient rule, as an identity rather than a table. For a word w over {O,E} write p_q = 3/2 if letter q is O and 1/2 if it is E, and e_t = prod_{q<=t} p_q, so J^t(n) sits at scale n^{e_t}. For letters s < t the coefficient of the phase variable theta_s inside letter t's phase is (k/2) E at exponent e_{t-1} - e_s, where E = prod_{q=s+1}^{t-1} p_q. Proof: letter t's wave is e(k J^{t-1}/2), and J^{t-1} depends on theta_s only through the chain of power maps between them; composing power maps composes to a single power, so the chain contributes exactly the product of its step exponents. The identity that makes this a rule and not a table is E = e_{t-1}/e_s, checked on every word of length 3..10 and every pair s < t -- 75768 instances, no exception. It reproduces the three monomials Paper B prints: (3k/4) n^{9/8} at (w, t, s) = (OOOO, 4, 2), C = (9k/16) n^{3/16} at (OOOEO, 5, 1), and B = (3k/4) v^{1/4} at (EOO, 3, 1). LEAN, 14 September 2026: `chain_rule` in PaperBChainRule.lean proves E = e_{t-1}/e_s for every prefix and every intervening block, over exact rationals, on the back of `iter_split` (the product over a concatenation splits) and `iter_pos`; `iter_nil` is its unit case. The three printed monomials are `printed_thm53`, `printed_thm63_C` and `printed_thm63_B`, each the rule evaluated at its own word. Kernel-checked: the axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, with no ofReduceBool. Not a density statement and not a contraction proof: it prices a coefficient, it does not bound a sum.

The E < 2 linearisation criterion of Paper B section 7, as an identity. With the notation of J-paper-b-defect-coefficient-chain, the squared-defect term in letter t's phase sits at exponent e_{t-1} - 2 e_s, and since e_{t-1} = e_s E this equals e_s (E - 2). As e_s > 0 always, the second-order exponent is negative exactly when E < 2: linearising theta_s inside letter t is safe precisely on that condition. The criterion is therefore not a threshold fitted to the words that happen to survive -- it is the point at which the second-order term stops growing, and 2 is forced by the squaring and nothing else. Checked as an identity on every word of length 3..10 and every pair s < t (75768 instances, no exception), with the sign of the second-order exponent agreeing with E < 2 in every instance. Positive second-order exponents at defects a kernel keeps exact are harmless because they are never expanded, which is why only the deepest blocked defect is tested. LEAN, 14 September 2026: `second_order` in PaperBChainRule.lean is the identity e_{t-1} - 2 e_s = e_s (E - 2), and `linearise_iff` is the equivalence the second-order exponent is negative iff E < 2, for every prefix and block; `no_linearise_iff` is the same statement from the other side, and `two_odd_not_safe` and `odd_even_safe` are the two smallest instances (E = 9/4 fails, E = 3/4 passes). The proof uses nothing about 3/2 and 1/2 beyond positivity, which is the content of the claim that 2 is forced by the squaring. Kernel-checked. Not a proof that any word contracts.

Paper B's meander constant is derived, not measured: it is kappa G(1) with kappa in closed form. By Wiener-Hopf / Spitzer, with P_theta(w) = 2^-d e^{theta S(w)}/M(theta)^d, sum_d z^d E[e^{-theta S_d}; survive] = exp(sum_n (z^n/n) a_n) where a_n = E[e^{-theta S_n}; S_n >= 0]. The walk is NOT on a lattice -- S_n = o log 3 - n log 2 and log3/log2 is irrational -- so the non-lattice local limit theorem gives a_n ~ kappa/sqrt(n) with kappa = 1/(sqrt(2 pi) theta sigma). The exponent then carries a -2 sqrt(pi) kappa sqrt(1-z) singularity at z = 1, whose coefficient extraction gives [z^d] ~ kappa G(1) d^{-3/2}, so the constant is kappa G(1) with G(1) = sum_d N_d/(2 rho)^d. TWO CLOSED FORMS. The variance is exactly the product of the two step sizes, sigma^2 = log(3/2) log 2 = 0.281046996501, checked to 1e-15; and theta* = log(log 2 / log(3/2))/log 3 = 0.488077132. Hence kappa = log 3 / (sqrt(2 pi) log(log2/log(3/2)) sqrt(log(3/2) log 2)) = 1.541814521. NUMERICALLY. G(1) computed with an exact integer mask and a d^{-3/2} tail settles at 7.07, and kappa G(1) is stable at 10.89 to 10.90 across d = 1600 to 12000. The measured c_d oscillates around that value rather than converging monotonically to it -- 10.757, 11.046, 11.034, 11.063, 10.566 at d = 1600, 3200, 6400, 9600, 12000 -- which is why an earlier reading calling 11.03 the limit was taking one sample at d = 3200. The oscillation is the same three-distance signature as J-least-peak-staircase-is-beta-ostrowski. What is proved is the identity and the closed forms; G(1) itself is a convergent series evaluated numerically, not in closed form, so the constant is derived up to that series. No bound moves. REFINED 18 September 2026 (certificate_increment.g_one): G(1) = 7.0606 with an honest band [7.0422, 7.0725], 0.43% wide, from an exact head to d = 3000 plus a zeta(3/2) - H_D tail weight; kappa G(1) = 10.8861, inside the 10.89-10.90 already recorded. The band is psi still oscillating at the cutoff, not rounding, and it is why no closed form should be read off these digits. WHY IT STAYS NUMERICAL: the tail is sum_n c_n Li_(3/2)(e(n beta)) over the Fourier coefficients of psi, so a closed form for G(1) requires psi -- which is exactly what MeanderShape asserts and nobody has. G(1) is therefore not an independent open problem but downstream of psi. Projecting those coefficients from counts to depth 3000 resolves the mean (c_0 = 10.66) and nothing else: the higher modes sit at a noise floor near 0.012, so these counts cannot decide whether psi is smooth or has jumps, and no decay law is claimed. FURTHER: kappa itself is the MEAN of an explicit profile rather than a limit -- A_n sqrt(n) is a function of frac(n beta) oscillating by 15 percent, whose mean is kappa identically and whose jump fixes psi's amplitude (J-paper-b-ladder-profile-is-closed-form). RESOLVED AND SHARPENED 18 September 2026 (J-paper-b-psi-fourier-is-the-orbit-series): psi does have jumps, its Fourier coefficients are psihat_k = -(2*theta*a_1/(2*pi*i*k)) G(e(-k*beta)) for k not 0 and kappa*G(1) for k = 0, so the c_n this row calls for are this same series on the rotation orbit and the closed form G(1) was waiting on exists up to the one constant a_1. With that, the tail can be computed rather than bounded: at a cutoff of 1e6 the oscillating modes contribute 1e-9 and the mean mode 0.021785, so the tail is provably mean-only there. An exact head of 7.043077, agreeing with the exact integer counts to 6.5e-9 where both run, gives G(1) = 7.064862 and kappa*G(1) = 10.892707. CROSS-CHECKED FROM A ROUTE SHARING NOTHING: G(1) = exp(sum_n A_n/n) by Spitzer, with A_n exact binomial tails to n = 20000 and the closed-form ladder profile for the tail, never touching N_d at all, gives 7.0649004 against 7.0648619 from the counts -- agreement to 5.5e-6, and kappa G(1) = 10.89277 against 10.89271 -- inside the band [7.0422, 7.0725] recorded above and about a thousand times narrower. Most of the gain is the deeper head; what the Fourier data supplies is the proof that the tail needs no more than its mean. G(1) still has no closed form, because a_1 does not.

At the zero-drift tilt (J-the-two-tilts-are-one-measure) that splits into the survival probability, of order c1/sqrt(d), and the endpoint cost E[e^{-theta S_d} | survive], of order c2/d because S_d ~ sigma sqrt(d) and the meander density vanishes linearly at the origin -- together the d^{-3/2} of J-the-meander-is-shared-and-supplies-paper-bs-polynomial. Measured: P(surv) sqrt(d) is flat from d = 400 at 0.66746, the ladder constant, settled (0.66642 at d = 200, so it is the deeper depths that have converged). E[cost|surv] d is 14.75, 15.65, 16.12 at d = 400, 800, 1600 and only settles near 16.53 by d = 3200-6400 (increment -0.017 at 6400). The product is about 11.03 at d = 3200. The depths meander_constant prints are still climbing toward that, so the printed sequence is evidence for the exponent as it claims and understates the constant. THE GAP TO FIRST PRINCIPLES. The Brownian meander gives the second factor as 1/(theta sigma)^2 = 14.936 against 16.53 measured, a factor 1.107 the continuum picture does not supply. CORRECTED: that is NOT a lattice correction -- the walk is not on a lattice, since S_n = o log 3 - n log 2 and log3/log2 is irrational. The missing factor is the Wiener-Hopf term G(1), and with it the constant is derived rather than measured (J-paper-b-meander-constant-derived). Measured to d = 6400, not proved. No bound moves.

N_d/2^d ~ C rho^d d^(-3/2) with a CONSTANT C is false. The exponent and the polynomial are right; the prefactor is an almost-periodic function of frac(d*BETA), BETA = log2/log3, and does not converge. THE MECHANISM. In the o coordinate the event is o_t >= t*BETA for all t <= d, a simple walk on the integers against a line of irrational slope. The step distribution is non-lattice, since log(3/2)/log2 = log2(3) - 1 is irrational, but at each fixed d the endpoint S_d = o log3 - d log2 lies on a lattice of spacing log3 whose offset -d log2 mod log3 equidistributes. The barrier is at 0, so the asymptotic sees the gap from the barrier to the lowest available state, 1 - frac(d*BETA). THE MEASUREMENT. c_d = (N_d/2^d)/(rho^d d^(-3/2)) over 20 consecutive depths keeps a spread of 1.069, 1.069, 1.067 at d near 1000, 2000, 4000 -- it does not shrink, so c_d does not converge. Binned by frac(d*BETA) it collapses: within-bin scatter 0.065 against an across-bin range 0.628, a 9.7x signal. Across disjoint depth windows the SHAPE is identical, per-bin differences having sd 0.0037, 0.0020, 0.0019, while only the LEVEL drifts, by +0.287, +0.124, +0.054 as the window doubles -- that drift is the 1+o(1) and the shape is psi. psi rises from 10.3685 at offset 0.05 to 10.9968 at 0.95, with one departure from monotonicity near 0.65 that the endpoint offset alone does not explain and that is presumably a path effect. THE SIGN IS THE MECHANISM'S, not a fit: larger frac(d*BETA) means a smaller gap above the barrier, hence more survivors, hence larger c. WHAT THIS CORRECTS. The recorded constant 10.90 is one sample of psi, and the recorded oscillation band 10.566..11.063 is psi's range -- explained rather than noted. J-theorem-six-one-threshold-is-slack quoted truth/(p rho^d)*d^(3/2) as tending to C/p = 17.28 from the samples 16.4, 17.0, 16.6; those samples wobbled because they are samples of psi/p, which ranges over about 16.4..17.4, not because of measurement noise. The sharpened upper bound p rho^d is unaffected, as is the d^(-3/2) exponent. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY PROOF ATTEMPT. A local limit theorem giving a constant prefactor cannot hold here; the correct target carries psi, and proving it needs a local limit theorem for a lattice walk against an irrational barrier rather than the non-lattice statement the step distribution invites. Machinery: surviving_log_mass, which gives every depth in one rescaled pass and agrees with the exact integer DP to 7e-15 -- consecutive depths are what makes the oscillation visible, and the exact DP costs 20 s at d = 3200 and overflows float beyond it. Formal layer in formal/Problems/Juggler/PaperBSurvivorAsymptotic.lean, which states the shape rather than proving it: rateBase_lt_one gives the exponential base below one, theta_beta_eq_rho is the rfl identifying this row's rho with PaperBChernoff.theta at beta, and theta_bound_is_sharp_up_to_poly packages the two-sided comparison beside the proved upper bound. MeanderShape itself is assumed, not proved. PSI IS A JUMP FUNCTION AND ITS JUMP SET IS THE ROTATION ORBIT (18 September 2026, surviving_prefactor_profile). The 'one departure from monotonicity near 0.65 ... presumably a path effect' recorded above is not a path effect: it is a discontinuity at BETA itself, the n = 1 member of {n BETA mod 1}. Sorting 100001 consecutive depths d in [9e5, 1e6] by frac(d BETA) at a sampling spacing of 1e-5, the twelve largest consecutive differences sit at n BETA mod 1 for n = 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 5, 7, 9, 8, 11, 10, 12, each within 3.13e-6 -- below the spacing, so every one is an exact hit -- with sizes 0.4214, 0.2230, 0.2154, 0.1718, 0.1210, 0.1169, 0.1009, 0.0778, 0.0751, 0.0695, 0.0671, 0.0630, decreasing in n. The median consecutive difference is 689 times the spacing and the largest is 42000 times it, which is a discontinuity and not a steep slope. This is the same jump set that J-psi-jumps-are-the-rotation-orbit-of-zero proves for the barrier psi via the Sturmian increment, so the prefactor's oscillation and the barrier cascade are one structure, and psi's range 10.37..11.21 here is consistent with the 10.3685..10.9968 recorded above. INSTRUMENT: surviving_log_mass is exact but O(d^2) and stops near d = 2e4, where these jumps are not resolvable; surviving_prefactor_profile narrows the state to a window riding the barrier, agrees with it to 1.4e-13, and reaches d = 1e6 in about thirty seconds. Two corrections were needed to make it right: the window must grow like sqrt(d) or psi silently decays instead of oscillating, and the denormal tail must be flushed or its unfaithful arithmetic migrates into the bulk -- at window 2000 and d = 30000 the total was wrong by a factor of two while window 1024 was right. No bound moves and MeanderShape is still not proved. AND THE AMPLITUDES CARRY THE SAME STURMIAN WORD. The jump sizes a_n at n BETA are not monotone in n, and their up-down pattern is exactly the barrier word: a_n > a_(n-1) if and only if s_n = ceil(n BETA) - ceil((n-1) BETA) = 0. Verified at every one of the 39 consecutive pairs with n <= 40 -- 39/39, no exception -- over 500001 depths in [5e5, 1e6]. So the jump measure is not merely supported on the rotation orbit; the same Sturmian word that places the jumps also modulates their sizes, which is the shape an Ostrowski spectrum takes. The amplitudes read 0.4245, 0.2182, 0.2259, 0.1747, 0.1196, 0.1238, 0.1037, 0.0778, 0.0805, 0.0698 at n = 1..10, the rises falling at n = 3, 6, 9, 11, 14, 17, 19, 22 -- gaps 3,3,2,3,3,2,3 of density 1 - BETA. Partial sums of |a_n| settle at 1.62, 2.29, 2.75, 3.07 over the first 10, 25, 50, 100, consistent with summability and so with psi being of bounded variation, as J-psi-jumps-are-summable-and-psi-is-bounded-variation finds for the barrier psi; the decay is not a power law but steepens with the window (p = 0.96 for n < 50, 2.61 for 50..150), the same signature that row records. WHETHER THE TWO JUMP MEASURES COINCIDE IS NOT DECIDABLE FROM THE PUBLISHED NUMBERS: the ratio of prefactor to barrier amplitudes runs 12.3, 14.3, 14.3, 15.9, 20.4, 20.4, 25.0, 43.7 at n = 1..8, but the barrier amplitudes come from 512 bins over 20001 depths and their smallest entries sit at that resolution, so the growth may be theirs. Remeasuring the barrier psi at matching resolution would settle it. Beyond n about 50 this measurement is itself contaminated -- the window half-width shrinks like 1/n and admits orbit points outside the sizing set -- and the amplitudes there turn spuriously negative; nothing is claimed past n = 40. Checked over every word of length 3 to 11: 4204 letters with a blocked defect, no mismatch on any of the three. Non-contraction is a condition on the same walk (1 <= e_t, i.e. u_t >= 0), so the property defining a contractor and the property tripping the branch-run hypothesis are one constraint at thresholds 0 and 1. At step two the first forces the second: a prefix not contracted by its second letter must be OO, since E gives u_1 = -1 and OE gives u_2 = log2(3) - 2 < 0, so e_2 = 9/4 > 2, the branch-run threshold, because 3 > 2^(3/2) (`noncontracting_two_forces`, kernel-checked; `two_lt_nine_quarters` is the threshold comparison). The defect with the largest amplification is usually not the one Paper B's screen examines. psi is bounded at every resonance that can be resolved, and the resolvable range stops well before BETA's hard partial quotients. THE CRITERION. MEASURED: at the convergent denominators the ratio |f_hat(q)|/||q BETA|| reads 4.57e-2, 3.09e-2, 3.19e-2, 1.75e-2, 1.21e-2, 3.62e-3, 5.08e-3 at q = 1, 2, 3, 8, 19, 65, 84 -- decreasing by a factor nine across the range, so psi_hat decays at those resonances and psi is bounded there. A DIAGNOSTIC THAT FAILS, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS USED ELSEWHERE. The deeper convergents 485, 1054, 24727 are out of reach at this horizon, and they are exactly where BETA's partial quotients grow -- a_9 = 23 and a_14 = 55 by J-cycle-period-bounds-are-one-semiconvergent-family. Can a Taylor series reach psi? No, and the Fourier alternative is the right tool but a slow one. NOT ANALYTIC.
