The jumps are directly observed (J-psi-jumps-are-the-rotation-orbit-of-zero) but the summability of their amplitudes is not, so psi is NOT claimed to be of bounded variation; the row id, written before the amplitudes were measured, overstates this and the statement governs. No power series in the phase exists, and a Fourier truncation at K leaves O(1/K), so this route cannot produce an error term better than polynomial. THE JUMP IS IDENTIFIED. psi's largest discontinuity is at phi = 0, of size 0.0736 against a next-largest 0.0268, and it is explained in closed form by J-paper-b-tilt-reduction-and-the-phase-factor: psi(phi) = e^(-lamStar(1-phi)) h(phi), and the explicit factor, continuous on [0,1], jumps by e^(lamStar) = 1.7095 on the circle. So the non-smoothness is structural and known, not mysterious. A secondary jump sits at phi about 0.633, adjacent to BETA = 0.6309; the Sturmian coding switches at 1 - BETA = 0.3691, where psi shows no comparable jump, so that second jump is not inherited from the coding's own switch point. RESOLVED by J-psi-jumps-are-the-rotation-orbit-of-zero: it is the k = 1 member of a cascade at every k BETA, and the arc endpoints are k BETA and (k+1)BETA rather than 1 - BETA. THE NAIVE SMALL-DIVISOR SCALING IS REFUTED. If Ostrowski small divisors drove the spectrum, |psi_hat(k)| * ||k BETA|| would be flatter than |psi_hat(k)|. It is worse: the spread rises from 18.8x to 153.5x, and the log10 spread from 0.334 to 0.436. WHAT IS TRUE IS WEAKER. The 1/k envelope accounts for most of the variation, cutting the spread from 15.1x to 5.2x, and the surviving modulation peaks on BETA's Ostrowski lattice: in both windows the five largest k|psi_hat(k)| lie in {8, 11, 16, 19, 22, 24} = {q_3, q_2+q_3, 2q_3, q_4, q_2+q_4, 3q_3}, while the five smallest contain none of them. Which five varies with the window, 16 and 22 trading places, so membership is the stable claim rather than the ordering. AN ESTIMATOR TRAP, PINNED. Averaging over the orbit itself fails exactly at k near a convergent denominator: ||q_j BETA|| is tiny, so the factor barely turns. At k = 84 it completes about 10 turns over d = 500..6000 and reports 0.34, three times the k = 1 coefficient -- an artifact that looks precisely like the small-divisor spike one is hoping to find. Bin first, then transform. CONSEQUENCE. The expansion route does not close J-paper-b-meander-prefactor-is-almost-periodic. It shows the target is only BV, names where its jump comes from, and refutes the scaling that would have made the Ostrowski structure tractable. No bound moves. RESOLVED 16 September 2026 by J-psi-jumps-are-summable-and-psi-is-bounded-variation, and the row id turns out to have been right: the amplitudes ARE summable, sum |a_k| = 4.58, so psi is of bounded variation. The caveat in this statement -- that the id overstates the claim -- can be retired. The spectral half of the tension was already dissolved by J-psi-reconstructed-from-its-jump-measure; the amplitude half is now measured over a 150-fold window instead of a 3.5-fold one.

An attempt to pin psi's jump amplitudes, which mostly failed, and what it corrected on the way. WHAT IS RESOLVED. With a slope-corrected estimator -- a line fitted each side of the jump and extrapolated, which removes psi's local trend as a plain window mean does not -- the amplitudes at k = 0 to 7 measure 0.074850, 0.038159, 0.019259, 0.019942, 0.015267, 0.010299, 0.010664, 0.008857. The same estimator applied at points off the orbit returns up to 0.00735, so that is the floor and everything from k = 8 down (0.00656 and below) is NOT resolved. THE APPARENT RULE, AND WHY IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Over the full depth window the ratio a_(k+1)/a_k equals 1.0355 at exactly the k where the Sturmian word s_k = ceil((k+1)BETA) - ceil(k BETA) vanishes, namely k = 2, 5, 8, 10, 13, with spread 4.3e-5; and 1/rho = 1.0352968. That is a striking coincidence and it is not evidence: the spread is across k sharing one dataset, not an independent error, and splitting the depths into three windows raises the spread to 0.19, 0.48, 0.43 -- the sub-windows cannot confirm anything. Of the five positions only k = 2 and k = 5 have amplitudes above the floor. So the rule is suggested at two points and the constant is NOT shown to be 1/rho. SUPERSEDED by J-psi-amplitude-ratio-is-one-over-rho-at-the-sturmian-zeros, which reaches seven positions by pairing nearest phases within one depth band and watches the discrepancy from 1/rho collapse 150-fold as the gap tightens; the constant IS 1/rho. What stands here is the floor of the sampling estimator and the softening of the bounded-variation claim. WHY SAMPLING CANNOT DO BETTER. psi's apparently smooth part is itself a sum of dense small jumps, since the orbit is dense, so no local fit separates a small jump from its neighbours. AN EXACT ROUTE EXISTS AND IS NOT FINISHED. Crossing k BETA turns b_(d-1-k) on and b_(d-k) off, so the barrier sits one higher during exactly one step and the amplitude is a difference of two DP runs. Computed at fixed d this is phase-dependent -- values at k = 0 read 0.174, 0.184, 0.045 at d = 2000, 4000, 8000 -- because the barrier word near the end depends on fract(d BETA). Getting a_k needs the backward/limiting formulation with the Sturmian word as input, which is where this should resume. WHAT IT CORRECTED. J-psi-is-bounded-variation-with-an-ostrowski-spectrum and Paper B's Remark 6.2 both called psi a function of bounded variation. The jumps are observed, but the summability of their amplitudes is not, and the measured spectral decay k^(-0.79) is SLOWER than the k^(-1) bounded variation would give. Both have been softened: psi is not claimed to be BV, only to have downward jumps on the orbit and to be discontinuous, which is all that the no-Taylor conclusion needs.

psi's jump amplitudes are summable and psi IS of bounded variation. The total variation of the jump part is 4.58, and since J-psi-reconstructed-from-its-jump-measure finds psi to be jump part plus unresolved jump tail with NO evidence of a smooth component, that settles psi. THE MEASUREMENT. sum |a_k| over k = 1..3000 reads 4.5800 at anchor Q = 3019940 and 4.5741 at Q = 6039880, 0.13 percent apart, with all 3000 amplitudes negative in both. The partial sums settle rather than diverge: 3.4032, 3.9239, 4.2126, 4.4169, 4.5001, 4.5431, 4.5670, 4.5800 at K = 100, 250, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000, the blocks [250,500), [500,1000), [1000,2000) adding 0.2887, 0.2043, 0.1261. The tail past 3000 is about 0.07 at the local exponent, so the total variation is 4.6 to within a couple of percent. WHY THE EARLIER EXPONENT READ -1.09 AND WHY THAT WAS NOT ENOUGH. The exponent STEEPENS with the window: fitting the same exact amplitudes gives -1.1273 over k = 20..69, -1.2204 over 20..200, -1.3932 over 20..1000 and -1.7654 over 100..3000. So a_k is not a clean power law, and the k = 20..69 window that earlier work could reach necessarily reads close to -1, which is exactly the boundary and cannot decide summability. h_k = |a_k| k falls monotonically by octave -- 0.8035, 0.8081, 0.7352, 0.6268, 0.4951, 0.3653, 0.2479, 0.1354 from [10,20) to [1280,2560) -- after rising to a peak near k = 30, which is why a window ending at 69 sees almost no decay. THE METHOD. psi is defined only at phi = frac(d BETA) for the matching d, so the two sides of k BETA come from two depths Q + k and Q + q + k with frac(Q BETA) tiny positive and q a left-landing convergent denominator. Two errors pull against each other: the depth ratio 1 + q/Q governs the 1 + o(1) cancellation and wants q << Q, while the phase gap ||q BETA|| admits every other orbit point inside it -- nearest k +- q -- and wants q >> kmax. At q = 1054 with kmax = 3000 only 38 percent of amplitudes come out negative; at q = 50508, 3000 out of 3000 do. The SIGN is the diagnostic and it is what caught three wrong parameter choices. VALIDATED three ways: against backward_prefix_ratio to 1e-12; against the exact rule a_(k+1)/a_k = 1/rho at the Sturmian zeros, reading 1.03530 at every one against 1.0352968; and between two anchors, agreeing to 4.4e-6 at k = 1, 3.3e-4 at k = 100 and 1.05e-1 at k = 3000. A COMPUTATIONAL CORRECTION THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ROW: the backward recursion's adjoint has ZERO net drift, so its support spreads like sqrt(d) and a fixed cap eventually truncates it. At cap = 300 the mean of psi over a decade collapses -- 10.5843, 10.8766, 9.6430, 5.0011 at d in [1e3,2e3), [2e4,4e4), [1e5,2e5), [2.5e5,3e5) -- while at cap = 1200 and 3000 it is flat at 10.5843, 10.8766, 10.8894, 10.8910, as an almost-periodic function requires. backward_prefix_ratio's default cap = 300 is safe only at the depths it has been used at, around 2.5e4, and silently understates psi past about 6e4. Machinery: psi_by_depth, which gets every depth in one O(dmax) sweep by the adjoint recursion instead of O(d) per depth, and psi_jump_amplitudes.

psi's discontinuity set is exactly the forward rotation orbit {k BETA mod 1 : k >= 0}, which identifies the unexplained second jump of J-psi-is-bounded-variation-with-an-ostrowski-spectrum and subsumes it into a cascade. THE MECHANISM IS EXACT. The Sturmian barrier increment is b_t = 1 iff fract(t BETA) >= 1 - BETA (PaperBTilt.sturmian_step), and fract((d-1-k)BETA) = fract(d BETA) - (k+1)BETA. The set {phi : phi - (k+1)BETA mod 1 >= 1 - BETA} is an arc of length BETA whose endpoints are k BETA and (k+1)BETA. So the barrier step k+1 from the end switches at k BETA, and taking the union over k the jump set is the whole orbit: countable, dense, with summable sizes. The k = 1 member is BETA = 0.6309, which is the jump at about 0.633 recorded as unexplained. MEASURED. At 512 bins over 20001 depths the nine largest jumps land on k BETA for k = 0 to 8 with no exception, each within 0.0006 of target against a bin width of 0.00195. Sizes from windows of width 0.02 either side: -0.07112, -0.03415, -0.01505, -0.01559, -0.01078, -0.00573, -0.00593, -0.00403, -0.00172 at k = 0 to 8, every one NEGATIVE. So psi drops crossing each k BETA upward and recovers smoothly between: a sawtooth on the orbit. The sizes pair up at k = (2,3), (5,6), (8,9), (10,11) -- differences of 3 = q_2 -- which is the three-distance structure of the orbit. From k = 8 the jumps fall to the level at which a window comparison also picks up psi's local slope (off-orbit controls read up to 0.0056), so they are not individually resolved and nothing is claimed for them. WHAT IT EXPLAINS. Both earlier readings, at once. Jumps give the k^(-0.79) Fourier decay, and a jump set which IS a rotation orbit gives the Ostrowski peaks, the transform of the jump measure being sum_k a_k e^(-2 pi i j k BETA). It also revises the attribution of the k = 0 jump: the explicit factor e^(-lamStar(1-phi)) jumps by e^(lamStar) = 1.7095 on the circle, but the measured net jump at 0 is only 7%, so h cancels most of it, consistent with the two-competing-effects reading. The jumps at k >= 1 come from h alone, the explicit factor being smooth away from 0. No bound moves; this is the structure of psi, not its existence, which remains open.

psi is reconstructed from its jumps, and that reconciles the two exponents that appeared to disagree about bounded variation. THE RECONSTRUCTION. With B_1(x) = frac(x) - 1/2, which drops by 1 at 0, the term a_k B_1(x - k BETA) is a downward jump of size a_k at k BETA. Summing the measured amplitudes with NO fitted parameter explains 91% of psi's L2 variation about its mean and 93 to 95% of each low-order Fourier coefficient (93.4, 95.5, 95.1, 95.0, 93.7% at n = 1, 2, 3, 5, 8). It saturates by K = 25: one jump gives 47.6%, five 84.3%, twenty-five 91.1%, and four hundred 91.2% -- adding amplitudes past twenty-five changes nothing, which is the same fact as their lying below the resolution floor of J-psi-jump-amplitudes-are-only-partly-resolvable. THE RESIDUAL IS REAL AND IS NOT A SMOOTH PART. It is 7.7 times the per-bin standard error, so not binning noise, but its spectrum is FLAT across n -- low-n mean 0.00175 against high-n 0.00134, ratio 1.31. Flat is the signature of the unresolved tail of small jumps on a dense orbit; a genuine smooth remainder would sit at low n. So psi is jump part plus unresolved jump tail, with no evidence of a smooth component. THE BV TENSION DISSOLVES. The jump part has psi_hat(n) = -S(n)/(2 pi i n) with S(n) = sum_k a_k e^(-2 pi i n k BETA), and this reproduces the measured spectrum to 0.3% at n = 1, 2, 3 and to a few percent through n = 8, with no free parameter. S is NOT bounded: |S(n)| ~ n^(+0.055). So |psi_hat(n)| is a 1/n envelope times a GROWING Ostrowski modulation, and fitting a single exponent to that product reads slower than 1/n without any violation. The k^(-0.79) of J-psi-is-bounded-variation-with-an-ostrowski-spectrum and the amplitude exponent -1.09 of J-psi-amplitude-rule-is-second-order-in-the-sturmian-word were never in conflict; a single power was being fitted to two factors, and the Ostrowski peaks already recorded in the first row ARE that modulation. This removes the disagreement but does not prove bounded variation: the amplitude exponent is still a fit near the boundary, and psi continues to be claimed only as discontinuous with observed jumps. Nothing here proves psi exists.

Going rational removes the driving, and what is left is discrete BES(3) -- which redirects the route rather than opening it. THE IDEA UNDER TEST. For a rational barrier the period-q map is a SINGLE AUTONOMOUS operator, so the driving that makes this problem hard disappears and the apparatus for one killed operator applies; the limit p/q -> BETA would then be controlled by J-barrier-rate-is-the-chernoff-rate-at-its-slope, which finds no denominator dependence. THE OBJECT, QUANTITATIVELY. The h-transform of the period map is a genuine Markov chain -- row sums 1.000000, the check that the construction used the unnormalised step -- with eigenvalue 0.105441 against the predicted rho^65 = 0.105505 and eigen-relation residual 4.1e-13. Its drift is c/m with c constant to three figures across m = 10..80 (14.69, 14.82, 14.54, 13.94, 13.05 per period at 41/65); the per-period variance is q BETA (1-BETA) = 15.13; and 2c/sigma^2 = 1.94, which is the invariant-measure exponent nu h ~ m^2 measured independently. BES(3) is Brownian motion conditioned to stay positive, so a killed walk conditioned to survive landing on it is the expected answer and the numbers say it is the right one. IT IS TRANSIENT. Return probability n^-1.26 over n = 40..320, still steepening toward the n^-3/2 of BES(3); the n^0.5 normalisation decays 0.103 to 0.017, ruling out null recurrence; partial sums settle near 1.5. This corrects the label in J-killed-chain-is-rho-null. THE REDIRECT. Operator renewal theory is machinery for R-NULL operators -- intermittent maps, where the chain returns infinitely often and mixes slowly -- so a transient Q-process is not what it consumes, and removing the driving does not hand the problem to the literature that J-no-exponential-weight-restores-the-gap's negative-knowledge entry says is missing. The object is a YAGLOM LIMIT for a killed walk and the reading is quasi-stationary-distribution theory. PARK on the renewal route; the identification is what survives. Machinery: barrier_h_transform. No bound moves and no fate is excluded.

The cocycle converges to its quasi-stationary family evenly in the phase, with no excess at BETA's convergent denominators. That narrows what a proof has to fight. THE MEASUREMENT. pi_d is the forward profile from delta_0 after d steps of the true barrier word; Pi_(phi_d) is the same map driven by a far longer word at the same phase, so their total variation measures how much a finite history differs from an infinite one. Rescaled by the local power, the values at q = 485 and q = 1054 sit at the median -- 87.9 and 99.6 against a median of 97.9 -- with the immediate neighbours 484, 486, 1053, 1055 indistinguishable at 84.1, 86.3, 98.7, 96.9, and the whole sample spread only 1.6x across 78 depths, 1.45x on the deepest window. A small-divisor obstruction would show as a spike at those denominators. There is none. CONSEQUENCE. The divisors enter psi ONLY through f_hat in the coboundary of J-log-psi-is-a-coboundary-over-the-rotation, not through the convergence of the cocycle itself. So whatever makes the quasi-stationary limit hard to prove -- the one link still missing in J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate -- is not a Diophantine problem, and the difficulty is the criticality recorded in J-rho-has-a-tail-variable-variational-formula rather than the arithmetic of BETA. Combined with J-killed-walk-forgets-polynomially, which ruled out Birkhoff contraction, two of the three natural attacks are now excluded by measurement. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The exponent. Fitted by octave it steepens -0.97, -1.04, -1.12, -1.27, -1.60 across d = 500 to 12000 and does not settle, so no power is asserted. It is a DIFFERENT comparison from the two-start forgetting, which settled at -1.985 over a comparable range, and the two should not be conflated: a first pass here rescaled by d^2 on the strength of that number and produced a quantity that grows rather than flattens.

The quasi-stationary limit is a genuine probability distribution, and its SHAPE is not settled by the horizons reachable here. TIGHT. Mass below m = 50 is 1.000000 at every horizon tried, and the mean converges to about 3.07 rather than growing: 2.799, 2.970, 3.037, 3.060, 3.068 at K = 500, 1500, 4500, 13500, 40000. Nothing escapes to infinity, so the pointwise limit is a probability measure rather than a sub-probability -- which was worth checking, since a critical killed process need not have one. THE TAIL IS THE SLOW PART. Convergence in the word length degrades with m: Pi(m)/r*^m reads 0.9416, 0.9418, 0.9419 at m = 4 across K = 5000, 20000, 60000, converged to four digits, but 4.26, 5.95, 6.41 at m = 32, still climbing by half. Any statement about the profile's shape at moderate m needs horizons well past these. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The double root of J-rho-has-a-tail-variable-variational-formula predicts a linear prefactor, Pi(m) ~ (m + c) r*^m. The ratio Pi(m+1)/Pi(m) does approach r* from above -- 0.652, 0.619, 0.608, 0.601 at m = 8, 16, 24, 32 -- and a pure geometric cannot do that, so the prefactor is not constant. But the implied c is not constant either: it drifts 1.05 to 2.59 over m = 6..26 at K = 60000, varies with the phase from 1.05 to 0.29, and shrinks as K grows. That is consistent with an unconverged tail and equally consistent with the form being wrong. INCONCLUSIVE, recorded so the computation is not repeated in the belief that it settles something. Two earlier readings within this same attempt were also wrong and are noted for the shape of the error: a hump in Pi(m)/r*^m marching outward as the square root of the horizon was taken for a refutation of the linear form when it is the tail still filling in, and the tightness check was written up as mass escaping to infinity before the numbers were read, which show the opposite. SETTLED 16 September 2026 by J-profile-is-linear-times-geometric-in-the-line-coordinate. The form is right: Pi_phi(m) = A(phi)(m + gamma - phi) r*^m, with the linear fit's residual falling like cap^-2 on the period map's exact fixed point. The drift in m that this row could not resolve is the forward iteration's unconverged tail, and the phase variation is the choice of measuring from ceil(d s) rather than from the line d s, which injects exactly -phi. Neither was evidence against the form. The tightness recorded here stands and is now also checked cap-by-cap: at BETA the mean distance is 3.46 at caps 400, 800 and 1600 alike, while below the critical slope it is cap - 4.94 and follows the truncation.

R's jump amplitudes halve exactly at every Sturmian zero, and the reason is one line. THE RULE. Crossing k BETA flips exactly two letters of the backward word, w_(k-1) from 1 to 0 and w_k from 0 to 1, so R's jump there is a difference of two word-driven runs and is directly computable. Measured at k = 0..21 the ratio a_(k+1)/a_k is 0.50000 to five decimals at k = 2, 5, 8, 10, 13, 16, 18 -- exactly the k with s_k = 0 -- and unsettled elsewhere, running 0.988, 0.773, 1.166, 0.895, 1.258, 1.415, 1.060, 1.388. THE MECHANISM. A non-rising step is m -> m + X, so m = 0 is reachable only from m = 0 and the update sends pi(0) to pi(0)/2; it also preserves total mass, so no renormalisation intervenes. A boundary PERTURBATION therefore halves, and R's jump with it. A rising step mixes in pi(1), which is why no rule of this kind holds at s_k = 1. Formalised as PaperBBarrierStep.update, update_false_at_zero, update_false_sub_at_zero and update_true_at_zero, kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. This is the exact companion of J-non-rising-barrier-step-doubles-the-count: a non-rising step doubles the count and halves the boundary value, both for the same reason, that nothing can fall below a barrier that did not move. WHY THE RATIOS ARE TRUSTWORTHY WHERE THE AMPLITUDES ARE NOT. Doubling the word length from 1500 to 3000 moves every amplitude by 1.2 to 1.3 percent. That is a COMMON scale factor, since both sides of each jump are run identically and for the same length, so it cancels in the ratio and not in the value: the absolute amplitudes carry the convergence error of J-boundary-fraction-is-a-step-function-on-the-orbit, the ratios do not. That is the reverse of the usual situation in this thread, where ratios were the suspect quantity.

d/ds log rho(s) = -log(s/(1-s)): the tilt that makes the walk drift-free is also the sensitivity of the rate to the barrier's slope. PROOF. Against a barrier of slope s the Chernoff rate is the Legendre transform of a fair coin, log rho(s) = -s log s + (s-1) log(1-s) - log 2. Differentiating, -log s - 1 + log(1-s) + (s-1) * (-1/(1-s)) = -log(s/(1-s)), the -1 cancelling against the last term. The second derivative is -1/(s(1-s)). CONSEQUENCE. lamStar = log(BETA/(1-BETA)) = 0.536207535136 already carried two roles that looked unrelated: the exponential tilt of the surviving profile, and through r* = (1-BETA)/BETA = e^(-lamStar) the base of its tail. This is a third that unifies them -- it is the derivative of the rate in the barrier slope -- and it is what converts a barrier error |BETA - p/q| into a rate error. MEASURED. Rational barriers realise it: the difference quotient between the 12/19 and 41/65 barriers agrees with -barrier_tilt at the midpoint slope to 1e-6, and the second-order term is confirmed too -- at 64/101, where |s - BETA| = 2.7e-3, the two-term Taylor matches the measured rate to 4e-5 relative. ONE FUNCTION, TWO DERIVATIVES. Write G(lam, s) = -lam s + log((1+e^lam)/2), so that log rho(s) = min_lam G. Stationarity in lam is the DOUBLE ROOT of J-rho-has-a-tail-variable-variational-formula: the minimiser is lamStar(s) and its exponential e^(-lamStar) = (1-s)/s is the tail base r*. The envelope in s is this row: d/ds min_lam G = -lamStar, and it is the vanishing lam-derivative that makes the envelope step legal. The double root and the slope derivative were recorded as separate facts; they are the two partial derivatives of G at one point. Verified at s = 0.579, BETA, 0.66: the minimiser matches barrier_tilt to 1e-7, e^(-lam) matches (1-s)/s to 1e-7, and the minimum matches log chernoff_rate_at to 1e-14. IN LEAN. `logRho_deriv` is this row and is kernel-clean; `chernoffExp_lam_deriv` is the vanishing lam-derivative that makes the envelope step legal rather than merely plausible; `chernoffExp_at_lamStar` is the identity that the exponent at the tilt IS the rate, at every slope; and `log_rho_eq` puts the closed form of PaperBTilt.rho into logs, over the definitions `logRho` and `chernoffExp`. All four print [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] and nothing else. What is NOT in Lean is the measured content -- that a rational barrier of slope p/q really decays at rho(p/q) -- which stays in J-barrier-rate-is-the-chernoff-rate-at-its-slope as a measurement. Machinery: chernoff_exponent, barrier_tilt, chernoff_rate_at.

Replacing BETA by a convergent turns the quasi-stationary profile into an exact eigenvector, which settles the shape question the iterative method could not. THE METHOD. For p/q rational, b_t = ceil((t+1)p/q) - ceil(t p/q) is periodic with period q, so the product of the q updates has a Perron eigenvector -- the profile -- with an eigenvalue giving the rate. There is no iteration error: the residual of the eigen-relation reaches 1.0e-18 at 306/485, against the steps^(-1.5) convergence that limited boundary_fraction_at_phases. And it is BETA's answer, not the rational's: 53/84, 306/485 and 665/1054 agree to five decimals on every quantity examined. THE RATE converges with the alternating sign convergents have, log rho(p/q) - log rho reading +3.06e-3, -3.69e-4, +7.85e-5, -1.94e-5, -6.14e-6 at 5/8, 12/19, 41/65, 53/84, 306/485. AMENDED: those are measured rates at a fixed cap, and a capped profile carries a bias of -pi^2 s(1-s)/(2 cap^2) -- see J-barrier-cap-bias-is-a-killed-diffusion -- worth -7.2e-6 at the cap used. From 306/485 on that bias is larger than the barrier's own error, so the last figure is mostly the cap and not the convergent, and the sign alternation it shows is the cap's rather than the continued fraction's. What the barrier alone does is J-barrier-rate-is-the-chernoff-rate-at-its-slope. THE SHAPE supports the double root of J-rho-has-a-tail-variable-variational-formula, which predicts a linear prefactor Pi(m) ~ C m r*^m. Fitting Pi(m) = C m^alpha r*^m on the exact eigenvector gives alpha = 0.980, 0.983, 0.974 on windows in m = 5..45, and a free-base fit gives alpha between 0.99 and 1.03 with the base within 0.2 percent of r*. The alpha-base trade-off is the usual degeneracy of such a fit and both sit within a few percent of the predicted pair (1, r*). SUPPORTED, NOT PROVED -- but an upgrade on J-quasi-stationary-profile-is-tight-shape-unsettled, where the same question was inconclusive because the tail had not converged from a delta start. What changed is not more computation but a better object: an eigenvector carries its own certificate, and an iterate does not. The constant-c form (m + c) r*^m is definitely wrong -- the implied c drifts 0.162 to 3.01 over m = 4..50, identically across all three convergents, so that drift is real and not convergence error. Machinery: rational_barrier_profile.

The renewal chain of J-live-set-ladder-factorisation conserves depth, as the split conserved floors. Coarse/fine independence at the OE renewal with ℓ forward letters is Σ_M μ(M)χ_ℓ(M) ≈ f̄ Σ_M |F_M| χ_ℓ(M). Summed over n instead of M, the left side is EXACTLY Σ_{n odd, x_1(n) even} (−1)^{x_{2+ℓ}(n)}·1[excursion from x_2] — the parity balance of the cylinder OE·w at depth 2 + ℓ, Paper B's object with no twist and no short interval — and the null is the same sum over all odd n for the counterfactual orbit of ⌊n^{3/4}⌋ (verified exactly, both identities, on 3000 fibres at M = 1e9 to depth 4: e.g. 4892/4892, 3804/3804, 13778/13778, 2635/2635 against nulls 4672, 3663.5, 13664.5, 2669). So the twisted-Paper-B formulation of J-first-renewal-density-three-phases is a HARDER proof of the SAME depth-(2+ℓ) statement, and Paper B's depth-4 theorem already gives the OE link for ℓ ≤ 2 unconditionally. In general a link whose ladder measure carries k floors of history against ℓ forward letters is the depth-(k+ℓ) statement: the damping lemma makes the measure's SUPPORT a single floor, but its DENSITY carries the full history at full frequency (the earliest segment's parities wind fastest across the fibre, so recovering them from M needs the highest harmonics), and chaining the links is the depth-d statement it always was. The Markov property a renewal argument needs — independence of a segment from the whole earlier history given the epoch state — is not a weaker hypothesis than fixed-depth equidistribution at the summed depth. Two prices recorded for completeness: (a) Paper B's own slow-twist localisation (Theorem 4.11, Lemma 4.10: total variation after differencing ≤ 2h|I|sup|g''| with h ≤ P^{1/12}) against the monomial twist a·(3/4)M^{2/3} gives variation (a/3)P^{−1/4} — small only for a ≪ P^{1/4} — while the frequency coordinate of the link needs a up to H = (4/3)P^{1/3}, where the variation is 2.5 (P = 1e9) to 20.6 (P = 1e20) and the twist's first derivative is 2/3; carrying the twist inside the differenced phase instead is a second-derivative perturbation of relative size ≤ (a/k)P^{−5/6} but a first-derivative perturbation of size up to 2/3, and in any case buys nothing beyond depth 4. (b) A supermartingale bound on the tilted mass epoch by epoch would need a uniform-in-state bound on the tilted excursion mass from a single state, i.e. the every-cylinder form of H(C,A). What the chain leaves: the E-absorbs-floor identity ⌊√⌊a⌋⌋ = ⌊√a⌋ makes every no-OO word an exact iterated ⌊·^{3/4}⌋ — which is the fate note's OEOEE route to λ** = 0.4801 (door 3), a human proof with no Paper B input, still pending.

rho has a second variational characterisation, in the TAIL variable, dual to the Cramer one in the tilt variable -- and the minimum is attained with a DOUBLE root, which is the structural reason a polynomial factor accompanies rho^d. THE SET-UP. In the m coordinate the conditional law updates by two maps: T_0 pi(m) = (pi(m) + pi(m-1))/2 when the barrier does not rise, and T_1 pi(m) = (pi(m) + pi(m+1))/2 when it does, the latter losing pi(0)/2. A geometric tail r^m keeps its SHAPE under both -- T_0 multiplies its mass by (1+1/r)/2 and T_1 by (1+r)/2 -- so along a word with density BETA of rises the tail reproduces with factor [(1+1/r)/2]^(1-BETA) [(1+r)/2]^BETA. Setting that equal to rho is the characteristic equation for the quasi-stationary tail. THE DOUBLE ROOT. The exponent is stationary exactly at r* = (1-BETA)/BETA = exp(-lamStar) = 0.584962501, and there 1 + 1/r* = 1/(1-BETA) and 1 + r* = 1/BETA, so its value collapses to -[log2 + BETA log BETA + (1-BETA) log(1-BETA)] = -KL(BETA || 1/2) = log rho. The minimum TOUCHES log rho rather than crossing it: verified to 5.55e-17, and g(r* +- delta) > log rho at delta = 0.2, 0.05, 0.01, 0.001. So rho = min over r of that expression, attained at the tilt. WHY IT MATTERS. A simple root would give a pure geometric tail and a pure exponential decay; a double root is the critical case and produces the polynomial correction, which is where d^(-3/2) comes from. The tail ratio of the quasi-stationary profile being exactly exp(-lamStar) also ties J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate to J-paper-b-tilt-reduction-and-the-phase-factor: the rate at which the conditional profile decays away from the barrier is the same number that makes the walk mean zero. LEAN. The substitutions are one_add_inv_tailRoot and one_add_tailRoot, the identification of the tail ratio with the tilt is tailRoot_mul_odds, and the first-order condition is stationary_iff_eq_tailRoot, with tailRoot naming the quantity; all kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. MEASURED, WITH A CAVEAT. The conditional profile's ratio pi(m+1)/pi(m) falls through r* from above around m = 60 to 80 and then continues below it, reading 0.5940, 0.5819, 0.5699, 0.5498 at m = 40, 80, 150, 300. That is NOT a grid artefact -- the figures are identical on grids of width 600, 1200 and 2400 -- but a finite-depth cutoff at large m, and it is recorded rather than explained. Nothing here proves the quasi-stationary limit exists. The same stationarity read in the TILT variable rather than the tail variable is `chernoffExp_lam_deriv` of J-rate-slope-derivative-is-the-tilt, where it is paired with the envelope in the slope; the two are partial derivatives of one function at one point.

The least-peak staircase's jumps are EXACTLY BETA's semiconvergents on one side, the cycle module's record lengths are exactly those on the other, and together they exhaust the semiconvergents. THE CONVERSE DOES NOT FAIL; IT NEEDS THE SIGN. J-least-peak-staircase-is-beta-ostrowski measures the jumps to length 1200 -- 2, 5, 8, 27, 46, 65, 149, 233, 317, 401, 485 -- finds every one a semiconvergent denominator, and records that the converse fails because 3, 19, 84 and 1054 are semiconvergents that are not jumps. Writing gap(d) = o log2(3) - d at the nearest o, the jump set to kmax = 26000 is EXACTLY the set of semiconvergents with gap < 0: 34 elements each way with no exception in either direction, and the four recorded 'converse failures' are precisely the gap > 0 ones. THE PREDICTION THAT TESTED IT, made before it was run. Semiconvergents come in families q_(k-1) + j q_k for j = 1..a_(k+1), and the families alternate sides. The family after 485 is 485 + j*1054 with j = 1..23, landing on 23*1054 + 485 = 24727, the next convergent. Length 1200 stops just short of its first member, 1539. Extended to 26000, all twenty-three appear -- 1539, 2593, 3647, 4701, 5755, 6809, 7863, 8917, 9971, 11025, 12079, 13133, 14187, 15241, 16295, 17349, 18403, 19457, 20511, 21565, 22619, 23673, 24727 -- with nothing between 485 and 1539 and nothing after 24727. A 21-fold extension of the measured range with zero exceptions. THE OTHER SIDE IS THE CYCLE MODULE'S, INDEPENDENTLY. The semiconvergents with gap > 0 up to 50508 are 3, 11, 19, 84, 569, 1054, 25781, 50508, which is exactly cycle_gap_baker.RECORD_LENGTHS apart from the trivial 1. So Paper B's walk geometry and the cycle side's Diophantine near-convergent lengths are two halves of ONE semiconvergent split, and 25781 was derived from the staircase side here before being found already present in the cycle module. This sharpens J-the-two-families-are-opposite-signs-of-one-approximation from a disjointness statement to a partition: the two sets are not merely disjoint, they are complementary within the semiconvergents. WHAT IS AND IS NOT PROVED. That one-sided approximation records are exactly the one-sided semiconvergents is classical. That the staircase steps exactly at those records follows from the mechanism of J-noncontracting-peak-supremum-log2-three -- the least peak is set by how closely a reachable level creeps below 1 - c -- but is verified to 26000 rather than proved for all k. MACHINERY. least_peak_staircase collapses the dynamic program to one array recurrence: the state (t,a) fixes the level u = a log2(3) - t, and that level depends on the NEW state alone, so new[a] = max(min(prev[a], prev[a-1]), a log2(3) - t). It reaches 26000 in seconds where the dict form reached 1200, and reproduces it exactly (difference 0.0 over k <= 1200). No bound moves and this is not a halt theorem.

The Sturmian driving costs nothing in the Yaglom exponent and four percent in the constant, so q -> infinity is benign. THE QUESTION. For a RATIONAL barrier p/q the period map is autonomous, so the driven problem reduces to the undriven one at each q and Ocafrain's 1/t (J-yaglom-rate-is-one-over-d) applies there. The irrational Sturmian barrier is the limit q -> infinity, and that passage is benign only if the constant c in TV(pi_d, Pi_(phi_d)) ~ c/d stays bounded as q grows. MEASURED, at cap 1600 and d up to 32000, over six convergents of beta = log2/log3 spanning three orders of magnitude in the denominator. Exponents: -0.9987 (12/19), -1.0231 (41/65), -0.9961 (53/84), -1.0040 (306/485), -1.0055 (665/1054), -1.0055 (15601/24727). Constants at d = 4000: 20.2174, 20.6369, 20.0926, 20.1271, 20.1156, 20.1158. The constant does not merely stay bounded -- it CONVERGES, the last two convergents agreeing to six digits. THE RESIDUAL SCATTER IS PHASE, NOT DENOMINATOR: sweeping a full period at fixed q = 485 moves c between 19.7211 and 20.5154, a spread of 3.96 percent, which is the same size as the 19.89 to 20.64 range across q. THE CONSTANT BELONGS TO THE BARRIER, NOT THE START, which is what has to be true for it to cancel and leave d^-2 memory loss: delta_0 and delta_5 agree at once (19.68, 19.65 at d = 32000) and delta_20, delta_60 climb to the same value once d >> m^2. IT IS NOT HOMOGENISATION. Averaging the word over the diffusive scale would need d >> q^2, which at q = 24727 means d >> 6e8; the q = 1054 and q = 24727 rows already agree at d = 4000. What makes the family uniform is that EVERY barrier in it, rational or irrational, is a bounded perturbation of the SAME straight line: |ceil(t*s) - t*s| < 1 for every t and every s, with no constant depending on either. That is far inside the g_n = o(c_n) regime Denisov, Sakhanenko and Wachtel (arXiv:1801.04136) assume for moving boundaries. A CORRECTED MEASUREMENT. At cap 400 the constant appears to slide 19.6 -> 17.3 over d = 2000..32000 with exponent -1.0886; that drift is the truncation, not the dynamics. The truncated operator's gap is of order cap^-2, so the free d^-1 law holds only while d << cap^2. Raising the cap to 800 gives -1.0182 and to 1600 gives -1.0040 with a flat constant. Machinery: yaglom_constant. No bound moves and no fate is excluded; what moves is the record of what the Sturmian driving costs, from unknown to four percent of a constant. The uniformity comes from ceiling arithmetic and nothing deeper: ceil_sub_self_lt_one bounds a ceiling's distance from its argument, barrier_diff_lt carries that to two barriers at different slopes, barrier_diff_le_one_of_close turns closeness into a difference of at most one ceiling step, and rise_mem_zero_one confines each rise to {0,1}.

The 1/rho amplitude rule is an exact identity seen through a normalisation, not an empirical limit, and this is the sharpest statement about psi's structure the laboratory has. THE IDENTITY. Fix a depth band and let d-(k), d+(k) be the depths in it whose phase is nearest k BETA from below and from above. Stepping k by one steps BOTH depths by exactly one, in every case checked. And when the Sturmian word s_k = ceil((k+1)BETA) - ceil(k BETA) vanishes, the RAW difference N_(d-)/2^(d-) - N_(d+)/2^(d+) is UNCHANGED from k to k+1 -- not approximately: the log difference is 0.000e+00 at 32 positions across two disjoint bands, d in [12000,20000) and [20000,30000). When s_k = 1 it changes, by -0.054 in log on average, with no position of that kind giving zero in both bands (k = 0 does in the second band alone, which is coincidence rather than an exception). WHAT IT EXPLAINS. a_(k+1)/a_k = 1/rho of J-psi-amplitude-ratio-is-one-over-rho-at-the-sturmian-zeros is this invariance read through c_d = (N_d/2^d)/(rho^d d^(-3/2)): one extra step of depth contributes exactly rho^(-1). The residual drift in those measured ratios, from 1.03523 down to 1.03474, is the d^(-3/2) factor and not noise -- which is why the spread tightened as the phase gap shrank but never settled on 1/rho exactly. THE MECHANISM, which this evidences and does not prove. s_k = 0 means the barrier does not rise between k and k+1, so the two configurations are translates: the same word one step further from the end. s_k = 1 inserts a barrier step and breaks it, measurably. WHAT A PROOF NEEDED, AND THE CLAIM HERE THAT WAS WRONG. This row said a bijection on the DIFFERENCE was required, because the two terms were supposedly not individually preserved under d -> d+1. That was asserted without testing and is FALSE: each term is individually preserved, to floating-point zero. The identity is now PROVED in J-non-rising-barrier-step-doubles-the-count -- a non-rising barrier lets every survivor extend both ways, so N_(d+1) = 2 N_d and P_(d+1) = P_d term by term. The proof is combinatorial rather than analytic -- unlike the existence of psi, which remains a local limit theorem for a killed walk against a Sturmian barrier and is untouched by this. A numerical agreement at floating-point zero across 32 independent positions is the strongest signal in this thread that something is provable.

A(phi) is not an independent unknown: the update determines the tail amplitude from the boundary fraction through an explicit multiplicative cocycle over the rotation. THE DERIVATION, which is algebra and is exact. J-phase-shift-is-one-update-and-R-halves makes a phase shift by the slope exactly one application of the update, Pi_(phi+s) = T_b Pi_phi / (1 - b Pi_phi(0)/2). Pushing the tail form A (m + c) r*^m through it closes in the same form: a non-rising step gives c' = c - s and A' = A / (2(1-s)); a rising step gives c' = c + (1-s) and A' = A / (2 s (1 - R/2)) with R = Pi_phi(0). THE NON-RISING MULTIPLIER DEPENDS ON NOTHING BUT THE SLOPE. At 306/485 the prediction is 1.3547486 and the five occurrences in fourteen steps read 1.3549281, 1.3549291, 1.3549301, 1.3549280, 1.3549293 -- agreeing with each other to 1e-6 and with the prediction to 1.3e-4, the gap being the cap and the fit window, not scatter. The rising branch tracks its R-dependent prediction to 7.9e-5 while that prediction itself varies over 0.8228, 0.8467, 0.8274, 0.8521. THE c RECURSION IS THE SAWTOOTH AND THE BRANCH IS THE RISE LETTER. c' = c - s or c + (1-s) is exactly c = gamma - phi mod 1, and the wrap occurs precisely when frac(phi) >= 1 - s, which is precisely b(phi) = 1. That settles the lattice-branch false trail recorded in J-profile-is-linear-times-geometric-in-the-line-coordinate: the branch was never something to guess, it is the Sturmian letter. AND IT REPRODUCES THE ERGODIC IDENTITY BY A SECOND ROUTE. For A to be single-valued on the circle the cocycle must average to zero, which reads integral over {b=1} of log(1 - R/2) = -(1-s) log(2(1-s)) - s log(2s) = H(s) - log 2 with H the binary entropy. At s = BETA that right-hand side IS log rho identically, to 8.3e-17, because the Chernoff rate is beta^(-beta) (1-beta)^(beta-1) / 2. So the cocycle recovers J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate's log rho = integral log(1 - b R / 2), which that row derives from the count recursion instead. WHAT THE PROFILE NOW COSTS: one constant gamma for the shape, and the boundary fraction R for everything else. The three unknowns the family started with -- shape, zero, amplitude -- are down to R, which is already the laboratory's clean coordinate. WHAT IS NOT PROVED: that the tail form holds at all. That is measured (residual 2.4e-4 at cap 1200, falling like cap^-2) and the Lean module says so explicitly; these seven theorems are the consequences of the form, kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. Machinery: amplitude_cocycle_check. The update is proved in both branches, update_true_tail for a rising step and update_false_tail for a non-rising one, and the multipliers they produce are rising_multiplier_base for the rising case and nonrising_multiplier for the other. The two algebraic identities the cocycle rests on are one_div_one_add_tailRoot and tailRoot_div_one_add, the two shifts at r = (1-s)/s.

The quasi-stationary profile does NOT close into a scalar cocycle: R remains an independent unknown. THE HYPOTHESIS, formed and killed the same day. After J-profile-is-linear-times-geometric-in-the-line-coordinate and J-tail-amplitude-is-a-cocycle-over-the-boundary-fraction the profile is Pi_phi(m) = A(phi)(m + gamma - phi) r*^m for m >= 1, with gamma one constant and A following an explicit cocycle whose only input is R. The profile is normalised, so R + sum over m >= 1 of Pi_phi(m) = 1 exactly, and that tail sum has the closed form A r* [1/(1-r*)^2 + c/(1-r*)]. If the tail form held down to m = 1 exactly then R = 1 - A r* [...] and R would not be an unknown at all -- the whole phase-indexed apparatus would be a single scalar recursion over the rotation, and the laboratory's clean coordinate would be computable rather than measured. IT FAILS, AND THE FAILURE IS CONVERGED. At 306/485 the residual R - R_predicted reads +2.33e-2, +7.12e-3, +3.52e-3, +3.52e-3 at caps 400, 800, 1600, 3200 for phase 0 -- identical at the last two to three figures, so it is converged and it is not zero. Likewise -7.38e-4 at phase 23, -2.76e-4 at phase 46 and +3.90e-3 at phase 69. WHAT THE RESIDUAL IS. Exactly minus the boundary-layer mass. The normalisation is exact, so the residual equals the extrapolated tail sum minus the true sum over m >= 1, which is the mass the pure tail misses near the barrier -- the complex boundary modes of J-tail-spectral-gap-closes-like-one-over-root-q, which that row locates numerically. Over 200 phases it runs -2.941e-3 to +7.318e-3 with mean +1.076e-3, that is -3.3 to +9.8 percent of R. AND IT HAS NO SIMPLE RULE on this evidence: not explained by the rise letter (means 8.7e-4 against 1.19e-3, with standard deviations 8.9e-4 and 2.25e-3 swamping the gap), and correlating only weakly with the phase (0.19) or with R itself (-0.16). CONSEQUENCE. The description of the profile costs one constant, one cocycle, and R, and this measures how close the first two come to determining the third: within about five percent typically, and never exactly. R stays the fundamental unknown, and the open obligation of J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate is not reduced by any of the day's structure work. Machinery: tail_predicts_boundary. No bound moves.

The tail recursion's spectrum is a double root at r* plus q-2 complex boundary-layer roots, and the gap between them closes like q^(-1/2). THE EQUATION. A pure exponential z^m is multiplied by a scalar independent of m at every update -- (1+z)/(2z) non-rising, (1+z)/2 rising -- so over one period of a p/q barrier the characteristic equation is ((1+z)/2)^q = rho_q^q z^(q-p), a polynomial of degree q. On the positive reals h(z) = log((1+z)/2) - (1-s) log z has a single minimum, equal to log rho at z = r* = (1-s)/s, so r* is the ONLY positive root and it is double. Verified: exactly two roots within 1e-4 of r* at 12/19, 41/65 and 306/485, and no other positive root. This is J-rho-has-a-tail-variable-variational-formula's double root restated as a fact about a polynomial. THE OTHER ROOTS ARE COMPLEX AND THEY ARE THE BOUNDARY LAYER. At 306/485 the nearest pair is 0.44893 +- 0.11047i, modulus 0.46232, decaying 0.46232/0.584967 = 0.790 per site relative to the tail and oscillating with period 2 pi / 0.2413 = 26 sites. THIS RESOLVES the residue J-profile-is-linear-times-geometric-in-the-line-coordinate records as unresolved beyond m = 1: that row measures a decay of about 0.86 per site with an unexplained wobble at m = 2,3, against a predicted 0.790 and a quarter-cycle of oscillation over that window. The two stopped notions of the reduction are ordered but not equal. With tau(n) = min{t ≥ 1 : J^t(n) ≤ N₀} the entrance time into the floor and sigma(n) = min{t ≥ 1 : u_t(n) ≤ −L(y)} the first passage of the exponent walk below −L, always tau ≤ sigma: Lemma 8.1 read at t = sigma says u_sigma ≤ −L forces J^sigma(n) ≤ N₀. Equivalently {tau > t} ⊆ {sigma > t} — the live starts are a subfamily of those whose depth-t word is L-bad — which is the containment Theorem 8.3, Theorem 9.2 and the collision route all use, and the only direction any of them asserts. The converse fails: the power envelope J^t(n)^{2^t} ≤ n^{3^{o_t}} is an upper bound and the orbit usually sits well under it, so an orbit can pass below N₀ before the envelope certifies it. Measured on exact orbits, 4000 odd starts per scale: tau > sigma never occurs (0 of 12000); tau = sigma at y = 10^12 and 10^30; tau < sigma for 12.3% of starts at y = 10^20, with gaps sigma − tau of 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8. The distinction is nevertheless almost free where it is used: the containment cost #{sigma > d}/#{tau > d} at the operative depth is 1.000 at y = 10^12, 10^30 and 10^50 for both C = 20 and C = 30, and rises above 1 only at y = 10^20 — so replacing the live count by the bad-word count, the shared first step of Theorem 8.3 and of J-collision-bound-half-exponent, is free at three of the four reachable scales. AUDITED 14 Sep 2026: the y = 10^20 figure was quoted as 1.037 (C = 20) and 1.026 (C = 32) from a single seed, and the statistic is seed-sensitive at the order of the effect it reports — over seeds 3, 7, 11, 17, 23, 31 at 4000 starts it spans 1.0185–1.0476 (C = 20) and 1.0000–1.0446 (C = 30). The honest reading is a loss of about 2–5% at y = 10^20, not the 'at most 4%' first stated, which a seed draw exceeds. Nothing above depends on it: tau <= sigma is exact and the direction of the substitution is unchanged. Note sigma is F_t-measurable and tau is not: sigma depends on the word alone, tau on the magnitudes, so only sigma can serve as a stopping time for the walk's filtration — which is why the repair of H_q stops at sigma and not at tau.

The complementarity between cycle record lengths and staircase jumps is forced by a sign, and therefore permanent. A cycle needs 3^o > 2^d: the CycleMin finance bound n ln n <= (6/5) L 3^o/(3^o - 2^L) is only meaningful when 3^o - 2^L > 0, so the walk gap o log2(3) - d must be POSITIVE. The staircase's binding configuration is a level just below 1 - c = 2 - log2(3), where both E and OE are illegal and the walk must take two odd steps; that level is (o+1) log2(3) - (d+2) slightly NEGATIVE. The two constraints read the same approximation error with opposite signs. Measured: all eleven staircase jumps below 1200 have gap < 0 and all six cycle record lengths have gap > 0, with no exception. Since a given denominator has one sign, the two sets are disjoint by construction, and this is a fact about continued fractions rather than about log2(3) -- the same sign split is disjoint for sqrt(2), the golden ratio, e and pi. CONSEQUENCE. The closed door recorded in J-cycle-records-are-the-staircase-non-jumps is permanent, not an artefact of the depths examined: no depth can satisfy both constraints, at any scale, for any slope. An argument hoping to squeeze cycles by charging them the non-contracting peak cost at the depth where they want to close is ruled out by sign alone, and cannot be repaired by going deeper or by sharpening a constant. Not a no-cycle theorem and no bound moves; it removes a route.

Paper B's zero-drift tilt and Paper C's theta_C are one change of measure in two coordinate systems, and Paper B is the level-zero member. Paper C picks theta_C so the unconditioned tilted mean endpoint sits at the barrier -L; at L = 0, i.e. C to infinity, that is zero drift, which is the tilt meander_constant works under and the minimiser of the MGF chernoff_rate computes. The tilt PARAMETERS do not agree and should not, because the papers tilt by different statistics -- Paper C by the odd count o, Paper B by the walk value in nats. On words of fixed length t, e^{theta sum X} = e^{theta(o log 3 - t log 2)} = const(t) e^{(theta log 3) o}, so the coordinates differ by exactly log 3: theta_C = theta* log 3, verified to machine precision (0.536207535 against 0.488077132 times 1.098612289). Closed forms: theta* = log(log 2 / log(3/2))/log 3 and theta_C = log(log 2 / log(3/2)) = log(BETA/(1 - BETA)). This is the fourth and last level of the correspondence, after the conditions (J-paper-b-screen-is-a-walk-condition), the counts (J-paper-b-count-is-the-level-zero-bad-count) and the exponents (J-paper-c-exponent-is-paper-b-rate-at-level-zero): condition, count, exponent and measure are the same objects at two levels of one walk. IN LEAN. `beta_odds` proves beta/(1-beta) = log 2 / log(3/2), the identity behind both closed forms, and `lamStar_beta_closed` reads off Paper C's tilt as log(log 2 / log(3/2)). The coordinate change is `tilt_coordinate_change`: on words of length t with o odd letters the walk value is o log 3 - t log 2, so tilting by it with parameter theta equals tilting by the odd count alone with parameter theta * log 3, times a factor depending only on t -- which is why the parameters differ by exactly log 3 and should, recorded as `thetaStar_mul_log_three`. All kernel-clean. What is NOT formalised is that these tilts are the ones the two papers' arguments actually select; that is the content of the rows they come from, not of this dictionary.

Two facts about where the no-momentum hypothesis puts its weight, and one about where the data are fair. (1) A prefix at depth t has exponent e = 3^{o_t}/2^t = 2^{u_t}; contracting prefixes (u_t < 0) map their cylinder many-to-one onto a dense integer interval, where the parity of the image is a block-counting question, while expanding ones (u_t > 0) have sparse images, the Piatetski–Shapiro-hard class that Paper B addresses at depth ≤ 4. The tilt at θ_C selects odd share p_C = 0.599 < 1/log₂3 = 0.631, so one expects the tilted live mass on contracting prefixes. It is not, at any reachable scale: by exact fair-coin DP the contracting fraction of the θ_20-tilted live mass at d = ⌈20L⌉ is 0.063, 0.188, 0.140, 0.247, 0.313, 0.373, 0.565 at L = 1.25, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, and the tilted-live mean of u_d is +2.8, +3.2, +3.3, +3.3, +2.8, +2.0, 0.0 — exponent 4 to 9 — against an unconditioned tilted mean of 0.585 − 0.050(d−1) ≈ −L. The reason is that θ_C is chosen so the walk's mean endpoint sits at the barrier, so conditioning on survival always selects upward paths; the crossover to mostly-contracting is at L ≈ 12, i.e. log 2y ≈ 2^12 log N₀, y ≈ 10^35000. So M_θ,q is, everywhere short of that, predominantly a statement about expanding prefixes with sparse images, and the dense-image counting argument covers a minority of its mass. On exact Juggler orbits (6e5 at y = 1e20) the measured split matches the DP to three decimals (0.365/0.364, 0.135/0.134, 0.213/0.213, 0.091/0.090 at t = 8, 12, 16, 20). (2) Fairness of the next letter on live starts does not depend on the class: on 1e6 exact orbits at y = 1e20, binned by u_t and separately by log₁₀ J^t(n) at t = 8, 12, 16, every bin with ≥ 50 members has odd share within 2σ of one half (worst |z| = 1.89, on 218700 starts), including the band 10^10–10^15 within a few orders of the floor (0.4978, z = −1.2 on 73872) and the band above 10^50. The smallest live orbits are not the least fair, and the expanding class is not visibly harder at this depth. (3) Consequence for the reset door: the recorded closure 'high-walk E-images are sparse' applies to the class that carries the tilted mass; the dense-image class where a counting argument would work is 6–37% of it for L ≤ 8.

The exponent walk of the θ_C-tilted live population is a meander above the barrier, and its endpoint is bounded at every scale. Under the tilt the walk steps +(log₂3−1) with probability p_C and −1 otherwise (mean −0.050, sd σ = 0.777 per letter at C = 20); θ_C is chosen so the unconditioned mean endpoint sits at the barrier −L, so conditioning on survival over d = 20L letters gives a meander with endpoint about one sd above the barrier. Exact fair-coin DP: writing the tilted-live mean as u_d = −L + c·σ·√d, the implied c is 1.044, 1.049, 1.054, 1.050, 1.044, 1.029, 1.018, 1.004, 0.997, 0.989, 0.983 at L = 1, 1.25, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16 — constant to 7% across a factor 16 in L — and the formula's stationary point L* = (cσ√20/2)² = 3.3 is where the DP mean peaks, at u ≈ 3.3. The mean crosses zero near L = 12; the 90th percentile of u_d saturates near 10–11 for L ≥ 10. CONSEQUENCE: the envelope exponent 2^{u_d} at which the no-momentum hypothesis puts its weight is bounded — median below 2^{3.4} ≈ 10, 90th percentile below 2^{10.8} ≈ 1800 — however large y is. On real orbits at y = 1e20, d = 20 the θ-tilted quantiles of log₁₀ J^d(n) are 31 / 92 / 830 (10/50/90) against untilted 10 / 31 / 277, reconciling J-live-set-tilted-fair (the untilted median is not astronomical) with J-tilted-live-mass-is-expanding (the tilted mass is). PRICING THE TWO OBSTRUCTIONS ON EXPANDING PREFIXES. The next parity on a prefix of exponent e is that of ⌊x^{3/2}⌋ over the depth-t image, so (i) the pure monomial sum Σ e(n^{3e/2}/2) and (ii) the nested floors both enter. For (i) the k-th derivative test gives saving N^{−δ} with δ = max_{k>e} min((k−e)/(2^k−2), 2^{2−k} − (k−e)/(2^k−2)): δ = 0.033 at e = 4, 0.0039 at e = 7, 0.00049 at e = 10, decaying like 2^{−e} — tiny, but since e is bounded this is a cost paid once. For (ii) each of the t intermediate floors contributes a sawtooth of polynomial amplitude n^{e−3/2}·(3/2)^{k} to the phase, and t → ∞. So the difficulty that grows with depth is the NESTING COUNT alone; the exponent is a fixed, small factor. That relocates the unbounded-depth barrier: not 'the orbits get too big' but 'the floors accumulate', at bounded magnitude ratio.

Paper C §9.3(c)'s Walsh expansion is labelled for the unstopped moment, and its conclusion transfers to the live one unchanged. The weights arise from factorising e^{θX_s} = a_θ + b_θ(−1)^{J^s(n)} one letter at a time, with −b_θ/a_θ = tanh(θ/2); that is an identity about the tilt and is independent of which n are summed, so restricting the sum to the L-bad words leaves every weight in place and moves the restriction into the sums: W_T becomes W_T^bad = Σ over bad n of the character. Verified by exhaustive expansion at d = 9 against the direct sum. Hence the per-letter down-weighting is tanh(θ/2) for the live moment exactly as for the unstopped one — 0.1954 at θ_19, 0.1988 at θ_20 — and it does NOT inherit the factor ρ of J-tower-threshold-two-readings. The reason is structural: the tower threshold was a ratio whose denominator shrank under the live restriction, and there is no denominator here. What the restriction does buy is the trivial bound on each restricted sum, |W_T^bad| ≤ N·p_bad against |W_T| ≤ N, which shaves the tail exponent by exactly e(C) since p_bad is of order 2^{−e(C)L}: at C = 20 the tail Σ_T |weight|·(trivial bound) falls from 2^{5.231 L} to 2^{4.657 L}, and at C = 19 from 2^{4.893 L} to 2^{4.367 L}. Both remain exponential in L, so §9.3(c)'s conclusion — high-order characters are exponentially down-weighted while the tail is e^{Θ(d)} and carries the high-depth information — stands for the live moment with a smaller constant. No manuscript change is required; the passage is correct as written and its label is accurate. CORRECTED 6 Sep 2026 (adversarial review): the 'shave by exactly e(C)' used |W_T^bad| ≤ N·p_bad as the trivial bound. It is not the trivial bound and is not unconditionally true. The unconditional bound is |W_T^bad| ≤ M := #{n : word_d(n) is L-bad}, with W_∅^bad = M identically; and M ≤ N·p_bad with the exact p_bad is STRONGER than Theorem 8.3's conclusion, since exact p_bad (0.106 at y = 1e20, d = 25) sits far below the Chernoff surrogate 2^{−e(C)L} = 0.609. Measured M/(N·p_bad) = 0.998–1.005 across scales — an equality in practice, not a reliable inequality. So the shave is conditional on H(C,A)'s own output, and the row should read: what M ≤ N·p_bad buys is the factor e(C); what the restriction buys unconditionally is only M ≤ N. The conclusion that the tail stays exponential holds a fortiori.

Product-shape bound on the restricted Walsh sums: |W_T^bad| ≤ K·M·b^{|T|} for a constant K, with b = 2p_C − 1 = tanh(θ_C/2) (an exact identity, since θ_C = log(p_C/(1−p_C))), M the number of starts whose depth-d word is L-bad. It is consistent with every floor proved: extending the order-1 identity by Jensen on E_bad[(Σ_s χ_s)^k] for even k gives avg_{|T|=k} E_bad[χ_T] ≥ b^k − O_k(1/d), so the floor at order k is b^k and not 1. It says nothing about M and so is not self-referential. Measured on exact orbits the per-order decay rate is r ≈ 0.30–0.35 at d = 18 and 25 (between the floor b = 0.199 and the trivial 1), with mean |W_T^bad|/M by order 0.315, 0.075, 0.014, 0.009 at k = 1..4 against a noise floor 0.008 at y = 1e20, d = 25. PAYOFF, priced honestly: it moves the live Walsh tail from 2^{5.231L}·M to 2^{1.118L}·M at C = 20 at the floor rate (2^{1.833L} at the measured rate). It does NOT yield P_θ at any C: P_θ needs the tail exponent C·log₂(1 + t_C·r) to fall below e(C), and even at r = b = t_C the per-letter slope log₂(1 + t_C²) → 0.0559 exceeds e(C)/C → 0.0503 — checked at C = 20, 32, 50, 100. So §9.3(c)'s conclusion is untouched either way; this is a refinement of the constant, not a route. The honest trivial units are M throughout; N·p_bad is not a legitimate yardstick (see J-bad-set-spectrum-cannot-win). Recorded as the one unclosed question on the spectral line. SHARPENED (loop iteration 1, 6 Sep 2026): the review's r ≈ 0.30–0.35 came from an aggregate fit dominated by orders 1–2 with the constant K folded in. Measured per order on 400000 exact orbits at y = 1e20, L = 1.249, the ratio mean_{|T|=k}|W_T^bad| / mean_{|T|=k−1}|W_T^bad| is 0.221, 0.183 at d = 16 and 0.227, 0.155 at d = 20 for k = 1→2, 2→3 — bracketing the floor b = 0.1988 — with orders ≥ 4 at the noise floor 1/√M ≈ 0.004. So the rate sits ON the floor, not between b and 1, and K = mean_1/b ≈ 1.6 fits orders 1–3 to within 15%. The conjecture as now stated: |W_T^bad| ≤ 1.6·M·b^{|T|}, with the caveat that orders ≥ 4 are unresolved at any reachable sample size. The payoff verdict is unchanged: even at the floor rate, C·log₂(1 + b²) exceeds e(C) at every C.

PSI'S STRUCTURE TRANSPORTS TO THE WEIGHT BASIS, WHICH IS THE BASIS THE PRIOR ART USES. This is a mirror of results this laboratory already has on the length side, not a new phenomenon; its value is that Hikawa's Conjecture 7.1 is stated in THIS basis at THESE depths, so it says precisely what his Theta cannot see. It is not a reconstruction: no jump-measure sum was fitted on this side. See J-paper-b-meander-prefactor-is-almost-periodic for the 0.518-bit swing and for why whether that fits his stated tolerance cannot be settled without the PDF. AND THE JOINT TABLE ITSELF IS NOT IN OEIS. THE TWO BASES ARE ONE COLLAPSE, AND THIS ROW SHOULD NOT BE READ AS CORROBORATION. Added 2026-09-20, correcting the framing above rather than its numbers. The weight-basis profile collapsing on frac(d log_2 3) and the length-basis one collapsing on frac(L BETA) are not two facts. THE SAME INTEGERS: W(d) = M[ceil((d+1) log_2 3)], checked for d = 1..25. AND THE PHASES ARE AFFINELY CONJUGATE, in one line. With lam = log_2 3, BETA = 1/lam and L = ceil(d lam) = d lam + (1 - frac(d lam)) since lam is irrational, multiplying by BETA gives L BETA = d + (1 - frac(d lam)) BETA; the offset lies in [0, BETA) subset [0,1), so nothing wraps and frac(L BETA) = BETA (1 - frac(d lam)) EXACTLY, not merely mod 1. Verified to 3.6e-12 over d < 20000, which is floating point rather than mathematics. TWO CONSEQUENCES. The map is orientation-REVERSING, so the weight profile is the length profile read backwards and rescaled. And its image is [0, BETA), so carrying lengths never visit the rest of the length-phase circle, which is why 1 - frac(L BETA) is the natural coordinate there -- the same quantity collatz_finance_mirror already uses for the cycle gap Lambda_J, and J-cycle-gaps-are-mirror-images for the Collatz/Juggler gap mirror. WHAT IT COSTS THIS ROW. The measurement stands and the numbers are unchanged, but it is not independent evidence for the length-basis picture; it is that picture in another coordinate. Cited as corroboration it would be double counting. What it is still good for is the thing it was measured for: Conjecture 7.1 lives in the weight basis, so stating the oscillation there says what his Theta misses in his own coordinate. The result is elementary -- a Beatty computation -- and is recorded for what it pins, not for difficulty. THE NEGATIVE WAS RE-TESTED AND SURVIVED, BUT ONLY AFTER A FALSE POSITIVE. A peer session corrected its own sweep the same day with the rule that A RUN SEARCH CANNOT FIND A SELECTION -- it had reported three sequences absent when two were selections from catalogued families. That applies here, so the triangle was searched again under other readings. Rows REVERSED returns A214494, T(n,k) = C(n,k) - 2 C(n,k-1), and the first 24 flattened terms agree, which is enough for OEIS to report a match. THEY ARE DIFFERENT TRIANGLES. The barriers already differ at t = 2, so the agreement is not structural: the counts simply coincide until L = 11, where our row gains a fifth entry the ballot row lacks, and from L = 12 the values differ, 85 against 55. TWENTY-FOUR TERMS OF AGREEMENT IS NOT AN IDENTIFICATION, and this one is recorded because the next sweep will hit it again and the name looks right.

The Yaglom constant is the diffusive relaxation time of the killed walk: c(s) = K/(s - 1/2)^2 with K about 0.348, and it diverges at the critical slope where the limit ceases to exist. THE MECHANISM, read off the update rather than fitted. One step of _advance sends the distance to the barrier m to m + X - r with X uniform on {0,1} and r the rise letter, so the drift is mu = s - 1/2 per step and the variance is sigma^2 = 1/4. A killed walk with drift mu and variance sigma^2 relaxes on time sigma^2/mu^2, which is the (s - 1/2)^-2.
